refs: BRV replacement market 2024 (checked on the BRV press release of 20 March 2025): about 47.5M tyres, up 6.8%. The consumer segment is about 45M (95%, up 7.1%), made up of about 41.0M cars and 4x4 (up 7.4%) and 4.1M vans (up 5%). Trucks are 2.465M. Channel shares for cars: tyre specialists including independent workshops 71.3% (69.5% in 2023), dealers and brand workshops 19.8%, Fachmärkte 3.4%, B2C online 5.5% (6.7%). The season mix (all-season about 36%, winter 38%, summer about 26%) is for cars and vans together. BRV figures are association estimates of sales to consumers, not a census. 2025 (BRV press release of 30 March 2026, checked): about 46.6M tyres (down 1.9%), consumer segment about 44.1M (down 2.1%), cars just over 40M (down 1.9%), vans just over 3.9M (down 4.2%), trucks about 2.52M; all-season was the only car type that grew (up 6.1%); car channel shares 72.5 / 19.1 / 3.0 / 5.5%. The research adds that car summer sales fell 4.0% and winter 7.8%, which BRV blames on pull-forward buying in 2024 after the snowflake-symbol rule from October 2024, and that BRV forecasts consumer sales down 2.2% in 2026 if the Middle East situation eases. I did not check those last points.
BRV managing director, around 2018: fleet and leasing is about 17.5% of car replacement
Roland Berger, 2018 (context only): about 50 German tyre wholesalers, top 7 hold about 75%
ETRMA publishes members' (pool) replacement sales; Germany-level pool and non-pool figures were not found publicly

Scope (changed in this version): the research recommends the 41.0M for cars and 4x4 as the headline, because BRV's channel shares are for cars; they had been applied to cars and vans together (45.1M). Channel totals are now the BRV share times 41.0M (29.2 / 8.1 / 1.4 / 2.3M). Adding the 4.1M vans at 75% specialists, 20% dealers, 1% Fachmärkte and 4% online (the research's assumption) gives back the earlier 32.3 / 8.9 / 1.45 / 2.4M, so those earlier figures are the cars-and-vans equivalent. Vans are mostly commercial (the research assumes about 85%), which lowers the commercial share of car tyres from about 29% to about 24%.

Supply side rebuilt, replacing the earlier 51.5M pool, 8.0M imports and 14.4M export. wdk's annual report for 2024 (checked) says: 'Bei Pkw-Reifen konnten die Industrielieferungen um mehr als 7 Prozent gesteigert werden'; the percentage changes of sell-in and sell-out were 'eng beieinander'; the market shares of the mostly Asian importers reach 'je nach Reifensegment schon bis zu 30 Prozent'; and 'Der größte Abnehmer ist dabei mittlerweile der Reifengroßhandel'. From this the research infers consumer sell-in close to sell-out (about 45M for cars and vans), with pool members at 32-36M and importers at 9-13M; for cars and 4x4 alone about 41M, with the pool at 29-33M, importers at 8-12M and wholesale about 24.7M. The model uses the midpoints, a pool of 31M and importers of 10M. Caution: wdk compares percentage changes, not volumes, and the 30% is a ceiling by segment, so the split is an assumption. The earlier 51.5M came from an ETRMA / Europool car-tyre figure of 46.8M (up 7%), cited through Pirelli Germany's reporting, which I could not verify; if it is genuine it probably includes deliveries to German-registered pan-European distributors. The 14.4M export was a balancing item, which made the earlier balance circular.

Trade data (quoted, not checked): UN Comtrade / WITS 2024, HS 401110, shows Germany with gross imports of 87.8M and exports of 53.1M passenger tyres. The research adds Destatis flows from a Hans-Böckler-Stiftung study: 85.4M imports of new car tyres in 2022, German car-tyre production of about 31.1M in 2023 (extrapolated from Q1-Q3), about 25M imports from South-East Asia in 2024 (wdk), 10-11M exports to non-European countries and an estimated 17-18M consumer original-equipment deliveries. These include original-equipment and intra-group plant flows, so they cannot validate the wholesale, import or export boxes.
Wholesale infrastructure examples (research file): Best4Tires serves more than 33,000 dealers and workshops with more than 20 manufacturers; Reifen Müller stocks about 500,000 tyres.

Later Germany research files (October 2026) reached different splits: about 75 / 25 of sell-in (delivered earlier and then replaced), about 70-75 / 25-30 by treating the whole tyre-trade channel as wholesale (not applied), then a file that repeated the 60 / 40 flow of 33.5M + 8.0M - 14.4M = 27.1M. The latest file, a validation of the whole model, keeps 60 / 40 (range 55-65% wholesale) but rebuilds the supply side from wdk as described above. No source publishes a wholesale versus direct split for Germany.

Corrections to the last research file: (1) it puts A.T.U. at 3.0-3.5M tyres, but BRV's whole Fachmärkte channel, which BRV describes as chains such as A.T.U. and Pit-Stop, is 3.4%, about 1.5M, and the file itself puts DIY chains at 1.5M; (2) it calls Ihle a small family business, but Michelin took Ihle over in 2014 (Tyrepress) and Ihle Tires had revenue of EUR 167M in 2022; (3) its volumes for Reifen Göggel (1.0-1.5M tyres) and Reifen Müller (0.4-0.6M) look far too low against their 2022 revenues of about EUR 490M and EUR 282M (EUR 490M over 1.25M tyres would be about EUR 390 a tyre); (4) its per-company estimates are branches times an assumed throughput per outlet, and the assumption runs from 5,000 tyres an outlet (A.T.U.) to 20,000 (Euromaster); (5) the named players it adds up reach about 25-28M tyres, which it compares with the 27.1M wholesale figure, but the market is 45.1M, so the comparison does not hold; (6) it counts 570 A.T.U. branches (A.T.U. says about 530) and describes reifen.com as a 37-shop Apollo chain, which I could not confirm. Its other estimates are not used beyond the card: Helm 2.0-3.0M, Pneuhage 5-8M, Best4Tires 1-2M, Ihle 0.5M, dealer groups 3-5M.

Wholesaler revenue, 2022 (Neue Reifenzeitung 8/2024 ranking of company disclosures, via Reifenpresse; covers all tyre types, not only cars): Pneuhage wholesale EUR 543M (group EUR 908M), Reifen Göggel about EUR 490M (firm's own data), Best4Tires wholesale EUR 286M (group EUR 508M), Reifen Müller about EUR 282M including retail, Ihle Tires EUR 167M. Reifen Helm is not in the ranking (B+B Reifencenter has belonged to Helm since 2021). Chain counts (checked): Euromaster Germany 200 franchise locations (L'Express Franchise, 31 August 2026; the file says 199); A.T.U. about 530 branches (Autohaus, 17 November 2025); REIFF had 42 stores in southern Germany when Bridgestone bought it in May 2020 (Tyrepress; the file says 40). Not checked: Vergölst 180 outlets, Reifen Müller 45, Driver 70, Pneuhage 893 outlets including partners, Reifen Helm 54 branches (a store listing shows 53).

Player volumes revised in the latest research file (all research estimates, low confidence). Vergölst is now about 1.7M tyres (range 1.4-2.2M) and Euromaster about 1.3M (1.0-1.8M), down from 2.7M and 4M, built from revenue instead of outlets: Vergölst revenue about EUR 330M with over 450 locations including franchise partners (Vergölst press release, 2024, checked); Euromaster revenue EUR 316.3M in 2023 with 228 own and 144 franchise locations then (research, not checked), and about 400 own and franchise locations in December 2024 (Euromaster press release, checked). The research converts revenue to tyres assuming tyre sales are about 65% of specialist revenue (BRV operating comparison 2023) and about EUR 95 net per tyre. That arithmetic gives about 2.3M tyres for Vergölst (330 x 0.65 / 95) and 2.2M for Euromaster, above the research's own ranges. A strong truck and fleet mix at Euromaster could explain a lower passenger-car figure, but I could not verify it. Driver / Pneumobil (0.4M) and REIFF (0.3M) are not re-verified. A.T.U.: about 525-529 branches and revenue of about EUR 1bn across all activities (research, revenue not checked). Its tyre volume could equal or exceed the whole 1.4M Fachmärkte channel, so BRV may count part of it under workshops; range 1.0-2.5M. Wholesale volumes use an assumed EUR 85 per tyre (from one Best4Tires data point: EUR 508M group revenue over about 6M tyres in 2022, via auto.news, not checked): Göggel about 5.8M tyres of all types, Pneuhage wholesale about 8.4M of all types and countries including supply to its own outlets, which risks double counting.

Ownership and list corrections. First Stop in Germany is run by Pneuhage: in 2016 Bridgestone agreed a joint venture in which Pneuhage takes 75% (Tyrepress), and Pneuhage was to run the 47 First Stop branches from 2017 (Eurotransport); I could not confirm whether Bridgestone still holds a stake. Reifen Ehrhardt is a Pneuhage brand (27 branches in 2017). Neither is listed here as Bridgestone. Reifen Burkhardt, a family wholesaler in south-west Germany with storage for 250,000 tyres and wheels, was bought by Goodyear (announced 27 July 2022, Tyrepress; a law-firm news item of October 2022 suggests it closed, not checked). It was missing from the card and is now listed as a Goodyear-owned wholesaler. Ihle: Tyrepress reported Michelin's takeover in September 2014 (merger review pending then); the research cites 2015, which matches Michelin's purchase of a second wholesaler, Meyer Lissendorf near Cologne, in July 2015, so 2014 stands for Ihle. Tyre24 / Alzura, Saitow and Gettygo are B2B platforms, not stocking wholesalers, so their volume is counted through the wholesalers behind them. Other wholesaler names from the NRZ ranking tags (the ranks are behind a paywall): Bohnenkamp (mostly agricultural and industrial), Baierlacher, Meyer Lissendorf, Gamma, Rad-Center Derkum, Reifenvertrieb24, Grasdorf. Not checked: Pneuhage group revenue of EUR 1.15bn in 2024 and wholesale growth of 32% in 2023, and Reifen1+ with 687 dealers and 721 locations and First Stop with 200+ franchisees.

Online: BRV counts 5.5% of car tyres (2.3M) at the point of sale. The research quotes Delticom's annual report for 2024 as saying experts put the online share of tyres sold in Germany at just under 13% (the same figure is given for Europe and the experts are not named); I could not open the report to check. Delticom's Germany segment revenue of EUR 241.4M in 2023 (Montega, via the research, not checked) would, at EUR 75-95 a tyre, be 2.5-3.2M tyres on its own, more than BRV's whole online channel. The research's explanation is that BRV records tyres bought online but fitted at a workshop under the specialist channel, so online-originated demand could be 4-5M (research estimate). The model keeps BRV's point-of-sale 2.3M.

Trade policy and concentration (quoted by the research; I confirmed only that the regulation exists): Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1540 sets definitive anti-dumping duties on passenger-car and light-lorry tyres from China; the research gives 4.3% to 45.3%, in force from 8 July 2026 for five years, with a parallel anti-subsidy investigation due to conclude in December 2026, and quotes Agence Europe on nearly 93M Chinese units in 2024, a 28% share of EU consumption. These measures could shift volume between pool and non-pool brands. Wholesale concentration: Roland Berger (2018) counted about 50 wholesalers, with the top 7 holding about 75%; the research puts Pneuhage, Göggel and Best4Tires at about 20M tyres combined across all types and countries.

Wholesale cross-check (October 2026): The five biggest names plausibly carry about 60% of the 24.7M wholesale layer. Nothing points to the layer being too high. See the Wholesale check tab for the figures, sources and caveats.
flows.scope: Passenger-car replacement tyres (cars and 4x4, excludes vans)

market.short: BRV's count of 2024 replacement tyres for cars and 4x4s (vans left out).
how: BRV, the German tyre trade association, counts about 47.5M replacement tyres sold in 2024 across cars, vans and trucks.
That splits into about 41.0M for cars and 4x4s, 4.1M for vans and 2.5M for trucks.
The model uses the 41.0M for cars and 4x4s only, because BRV's channel shares are measured on cars. Vans are left out.
market.src: BRV press release of 20 March 2025 (checked earlier). BRV figures are association estimates of sales to consumers, not a census.

sure.w: Published by BRV. The 47.5M total was confirmed again in the news article above; the 41.0M cars-and-4x4 line comes from the BRV press release, checked earlier but not re-found today.

market.why: BRV is the one body that counts the whole German replacement market, so its figure is the natural anchor. The only choice made is to leave out vans and trucks, so the total matches BRV's own channel shares.
market.val: The BRV total (47.5M) is confirmed in the quoted article. Sanity check: 41.0M ÷ 49.3M cars on the road (KBA) = 0.83 tyres per car, in line with Spain (0.80) and Austria (0.86) in this dashboard.

industry.short: An estimate: about 31M of the 41M comes from the pool brands (range 29–33M).
how: No public figure exists for what the ETRMA pool brands sold in Germany (not found).
The research reasoned from the wdk annual report: manufacturers' deliveries and sales to consumers grew by about the same in 2024 (“eng beieinander”), so deliveries ≈ consumer sales.
Importers outside the pool hold up to 30% of some tyre segments, about 10M of the 41M here. That leaves about 31M for the pool.
Check: 31.0M pool + 10.0M imports = 41.0M market.
industry.src: Research estimate based on the wdk annual report 2024 (quotes checked). The level is an assumption.

sure.w: wdk compares percentage changes, not volumes, so the level is an assumption. Replace it with your own ETRMA Germany pool figure if you have one.

industry.why: If manufacturers' deliveries and consumer sales move together (wdk says they did in 2024), the pool's volume is the market minus what importers outside the pool supply. Neither part is published, so both are judgements.
industry.val: Quickest check: ETRMA's Germany pool figure, as you supplied for the Netherlands. Until then the only test is that pool 31.0M + imports 10.0M = BRV's 41.0M, which holds by construction, so it is not independent proof.

import.short: About 24% of the market (10M, range 8–12M) is bought from importers outside the pool.
how: Importers outside the pool, mostly Asian brands, bring tyres to German wholesalers.
wdk says their market share is already up to 30% in some tyre segments. That is a ceiling for the biggest segment, not an average.
The research takes about 24% of the 41.0M, which is about 10M (range 8–12M).
import.src: Research estimate based on the wdk annual report 2024 (quote checked).

sure.w: The 30% is a ceiling by segment, not a published average, so the 10M is a judgement call.

import.why: Wdk says importers outside the pool already take up to 30% of some segments. That is a ceiling for the busiest segments, so the research uses a lower overall share of 24%.
import.val: wdk's 30% is a ceiling for some segments, not an average, so the 24% cannot be confirmed from published data. Check: ETRMA's pool volume for Germany; market minus pool is the non-pool volume.

export.short: Set to zero. Cross-border wholesale trade exists but is not measured.
how: No German figure for wholesalers re-exporting replacement tyres was found.

Customs shows very large gross flows (87.8M tyres imported, 53.1M exported in 2024, UN Comtrade as quoted, not checked), but they include factory and original-equipment flows, so they cannot be used here.
The model therefore sets export to 0.0M. Real cross-border wholesale (for example Göggel selling to Austria, Switzerland and France) is not netted.
export.src: Model convention. An earlier 14.4M was a balancing figure with no source and was removed.

sure.w: A convention, not a measurement.

export.why: A figure with no source is safer left at zero than guessed. The cost is that cross-border wholesale, for example sales to Austria or Switzerland, is not netted.
export.val: Customs data (87.8M tyres imported and 53.1M exported in 2024, UN Comtrade as quoted, not checked) are mostly factory and original-equipment flows, far too big to be this box. Ask your German distributors how much they re-export.

direct.short: About 40% of the market (16.3M) is assumed to reach the channels without a wholesaler.

market.source: Research estimate, medium confidence: total passenger-car (tourisme plus 4x4/SUV, vans excluded) replacement sell-in in France in 2024, 37.1M (range 35.3-39.2M). It is the Europool sell-in of 28.9M plus an estimated 8.2M of non-pool imports. In TC4 units (cars, 4x4/SUV and vans) the same estimate is 40.7M (38.7-42.9M). Cross-checks, all quoted by the research and not checked: ADEME's 42.2M light-vehicle replacement tyres placed on the market in 2022 (cited by the Syndicat du Pneu), a vehicle-km wear model (about 540bn km x 4 tyres / 45-55k km of tread life = 39-48M, the research's arithmetic) and the market-share claims of Allopneus and Distri Cash. Replaces the earlier 17.211M, which is the Syndicat du Pneu/GfK sell-out of two panelled channels only (see Sources and notes).

industry.source: Europool sell-in to the French trade in 2024: 31.744M TC4 tyres, +4.5%, the Syndicat du Pneu/GfK 'sell-in' from manufacturers to resellers (checked on Journal de l'Automobile and J2R). The research's split, quoted from L'argus and the Syndicat and not checked, is tourisme 25.64M, 4x4/SUV 3.29M and camionnette 2.81M (these add up to 31.74M); tourisme plus 4x4/SUV gives 28.9M of passenger-car tyres. Europool covers members with EU industrial activity; the Syndicat says not every manufacturer reports to Europool, so non-EU, mostly Asian, suppliers are outside it (research quote, not checked). Replaces the earlier 13.0M, which was normalised onto the 17.2M panel.

import.source: Research estimate, low-medium confidence, range 6.5-10.3M: non-pool imports (non-declaring, mostly Asian budget brands), about 22% of the total (range 18-26%); 8.95M on the TC4 basis. Support: budget brands were 19.1% of the 2024 market (J2R, checked); the research cites ADEME's 2022 gap between 42.2M placed on the market and about 31.6M of Europool sell-in (about 25%; the 2022 sell-in of 31.625M is confirmed on Journal de l'Automobile, the ADEME figure is not checked) and the European Commission's finding that China supplied 28% of EU passenger and light-truck tyre consumption in 2024 (not checked). This estimate is the main driver of the full-market figure. Replaces the earlier 4.2M. The model has no imports-to-direct flow, so all 8.2M is shown going through wholesale (see the box note).

export.source: Model convention. The research treats exports and re-exports by French wholesalers (Distri Cash, for example) as not zero but unquantified, a possible 0.3-1.0M overstatement within the total. ADEME counts the first placer on the market, so the placement figures are not a clean net of exports. Replaces the earlier netting of exports into the import box.

direct.source: Research estimate, low confidence: about 58% of the 37.1M reaches the channels directly (21.6M). That is 19.9M of Europool volume (manufacturer-owned networks such as Euromaster, Speedy, First Stop, BestDrive and Allopneus, and the central purchasing of auto-centres) plus about 1.7M of non-pool volume bought direct by networks and online sellers. The model has no imports-to-direct flow, so the whole 21.6M is shown as the direct box and the import box goes entirely through wholesale; pool to wholesale therefore reads 7.3M (the research has 9.0M). Equals the sum of the channel direct figures. Replaces the earlier 8.0M (46% of the 17.2M).

ch.auto.tot.source: Research estimate, medium-high confidence: the Syndicat du Pneu/GfK panel sell-out of auto-centres and fast-fitters, 8.86M TC4 (27.9% of the 31.74M sell-in; research figure, not checked), times about 97% passenger car = 8.6M. Hypermarket auto-centres are counted here (the Syndicat's centres auto are 'issus de la grande distribution'); Leclerc's panel coverage is not confirmed. Replaces the earlier 4.80M, which applied the 27.9% share to the 17.2M.

ch.auto.ws.source: Research estimate, about 12% via wholesale (was 35%). Auto-centres buy mostly direct or through central purchasing. Calibrated so the channels add up to 15.5M via wholesale and 21.6M direct. Not published.

ch.auto.dir.source: Research estimate: channel total minus via wholesale. Central purchasing and direct supply to Norauto, Midas, Feu Vert, Speedy and the Leclerc and ITM centres. Not published.

ch.auto.prv.source: Research estimate of private demand by channel, about 78% overall (29.0M of 37.1M, the same as the earlier 78%). No French source publishes private versus commercial by channel; the only evidence is the GfK figure cited by the Syndicat du Pneu that about 4M of roughly 25M car tyres in 2023 were sold B2B by pneumaticiens (research, not checked).

ch.auto.com.source: Research estimate of commercial demand by channel, about 22% overall (8.1M of 37.1M). No French source publishes it by channel. Highest at pneumaticiens (about 54%: Euromaster is about 40 / 60 private versus commercial, fleet and leasing heavy) and lowest at online and auto-centres (about 8% and 12%).

ch.deal.tot.source: Research residual, low confidence: car dealers and independent repairers (MRA), which are not in the Syndicat's panel. On the Syndicat's own pool-only basis this block is 8.85M TC4, about 8.3M passenger car, and the Syndicat itself estimates 8-9M (research quote, not checked). On the full-market basis, dealers and MRA (14.0M) plus foreign online (2.5M) make 16.5M non-panel, about 8.2M more than on the Syndicat's convention, which the research attributes to non-pool volume reaching garages through wholesalers. This is the biggest uncertainty in the model. MRA still hold the first replacement of 4x4/SUV tyres (J2R, checked). Replaces the earlier 4.82M.

ch.deal.ws.source: Research estimate, about 79% via wholesale (was 85%): a long tail of independent multibrand garages and dealers supplied by wholesalers such as Distri Cash, AAG and PHE. OEM parts programmes are the other route. Not published.

ch.deal.dir.source: Research estimate: channel total minus via wholesale. OEM parts programmes and direct importer supply. Not published.

ch.deal.prv.source: Research estimate of private demand by channel, about 78% overall (29.0M of 37.1M, the same as the earlier 78%). No French source publishes private versus commercial by channel; the only evidence is the GfK figure cited by the Syndicat du Pneu that about 4M of roughly 25M car tyres in 2023 were sold B2B by pneumaticiens (research, not checked).

ch.deal.com.source: Research estimate of commercial demand by channel, about 22% overall (8.1M of 37.1M). No French source publishes it by channel. Highest at pneumaticiens (about 54%: Euromaster is about 40 / 60 private versus commercial, fleet and leasing heavy) and lowest at online and auto-centres (about 8% and 12%).

ch.spec.tot.source: Research estimate, medium-low confidence: the panel sell-out of tyre specialists (pneumaticiens), 8.35M TC4 (26.3% of the sell-in; research figure, not checked), times about 80% passenger car = 6.9M, because camionnette is concentrated in pneumaticiens. GfK data cited by the Syndicat say about 4M tourisme tyres were sold B2B by pneumaticiens in 2023 (research, not checked). Replaces the earlier 4.52M.

ch.spec.ws.source: Research estimate, about 17% via wholesale (was 50%). Euromaster, First Stop, Côté Route, Eurotyre and BestDrive are manufacturer-led and buy direct; Point S buys through Viasso's central purchasing. Not published.

ch.spec.dir.source: Research estimate: channel total minus via wholesale. Manufacturer-led networks (Euromaster, First Stop, Côté Route, Eurotyre, BestDrive) and Point S through Viasso. Not published.

ch.spec.prv.source: Research estimate of private demand by channel, about 78% overall (29.0M of 37.1M, the same as the earlier 78%). No French source publishes private versus commercial by channel; the only evidence is the GfK figure cited by the Syndicat du Pneu that about 4M of roughly 25M car tyres in 2023 were sold B2B by pneumaticiens (research, not checked).

ch.spec.com.source: Research estimate of commercial demand by channel, about 22% overall (8.1M of 37.1M). No French source publishes it by channel. Highest at pneumaticiens (about 54%: Euromaster is about 40 / 60 private versus commercial, fleet and leasing heavy) and lowest at online and auto-centres (about 8% and 12%).

ch.onl.tot.source: Research estimate, medium confidence: French pure players' panel sell-out of 5.68M TC4 (+21.9% in 2024; J2R and Journal de l'Automobile report about 5.6M, checked) times about 88% passenger car = 5.1M. French pure players only: foreign e-tailers are not panelled and sit in the foreign online box. Replaces the earlier 3.10M, which applied the 18% share to the 17.2M.

ch.onl.ws.source: Research estimate, about 25% via wholesale (was 40%). Allopneus buys direct from manufacturers and 1001pneus sources through Massa. Not published.

ch.onl.dir.source: Research estimate: channel total minus via wholesale. Allopneus buys direct from manufacturers. Not published.

ch.onl.prv.source: Research estimate of private demand by channel, about 78% overall (29.0M of 37.1M, the same as the earlier 78%). No French source publishes private versus commercial by channel; the only evidence is the GfK figure cited by the Syndicat du Pneu that about 4M of roughly 25M car tyres in 2023 were sold B2B by pneumaticiens (research, not checked).

ch.onl.com.source: Research estimate of commercial demand by channel, about 22% overall (8.1M of 37.1M). No French source publishes it by channel. Highest at pneumaticiens (about 54%: Euromaster is about 40 / 60 private versus commercial, fleet and leasing heavy) and lowest at online and auto-centres (about 8% and 12%).

ch.fon.tot.source: Research residual split, low confidence: foreign e-tailers and marketplaces (123pneus by Delticom, for example) are not panelled by the Syndicat, so they sit inside the non-panel plug. The 2.5M is an allocation, not a measurement. Delticom has a voluntary Aliapur agreement for tyres its clients place on the French market (research, not checked). New channel in this version.

ch.fon.ws.source: Research estimate, 40% via wholesale, a residual split. Not published.

ch.fon.dir.source: Research estimate: channel total minus via wholesale. Not published.

ch.fon.prv.source: Research estimate of private demand by channel, about 78% overall (29.0M of 37.1M, the same as the earlier 78%). No French source publishes private versus commercial by channel; the only evidence is the GfK figure cited by the Syndicat du Pneu that about 4M of roughly 25M car tyres in 2023 were sold B2B by pneumaticiens (research, not checked).

ch.fon.com.source: Research estimate of commercial demand by channel, about 22% overall (8.1M of 37.1M). No French source publishes it by channel. Highest at pneumaticiens (about 54%: Euromaster is about 40 / 60 private versus commercial, fleet and leasing heavy) and lowest at online and auto-centres (about 8% and 12%).

meta.boxNote: Boxes are the channels as named under "By channel". Industry is Europool's published sell-in (28.9M of passenger-car tyres); the import box is the research's estimate of non-pool supply (8.2M), not gross customs imports. The research sends about 1.7M of the non-pool volume straight to channels. The model has no such flow, so the whole 8.2M is shown going through wholesale and that 1.7M sits in the direct box instead; pool to wholesale therefore reads 7.3M, not the research's 9.0M. Export is set to zero; the research sees 0.3-1.0M of possible re-exports. Dealers and independent repairers and foreign online are residuals, not measurements. Private and commercial are research estimates by channel and no source publishes them.
meta.scopeNote: The 37.1M is a passenger-car (tourisme plus 4x4/SUV) estimate of total replacement sell-in, not the 17.2M shown before. That 17.2M is the Syndicat du Pneu/GfK 2024 sell-out of two panelled channels (auto-centres and pneumaticiens) in TC4 units (cars, 4x4/SUV and vans); it leaves out French pure players, dealers and independent repairers and foreign online sellers. In TC4 units the same total estimate is 40.7M. Europool's published sell-in (31.74M TC4, 28.9M passenger car) is the pool; the non-pool 8.2M is an estimate (range 6.5-10.3M). The three panelled channels are measured; dealers and independent repairers (14.0M) and foreign online (2.5M) are the plug.
meta.walkNote: The model has no flow for non-pool imports going straight to the channels. So all 8.2M of imports are shown going through wholesale, and the 1.7M that really goes direct sits in the Direct box. That is why “industry sold to wholesale” reads 7.3M, not the research's 9.0M. Wholesale (15.5M) and direct (21.6M) are the research's totals.

channels.why: Three channels are measured by the Syndicat du Pneu/GfK panel (auto-centres, tyre specialists, French pure players). Dealers and independent repairers and foreign webshops are plugs that fill the gap to the 37.1M market.
channels.val: The panel headline and the pure-player figure are in the quotes kept. The channel split of the panel is the research's reading and was not checked. The dealer plug is the biggest uncertainty.

refs: Method (replaced with the newest France research file, October 2026): the model is rebuilt on a passenger-car sell-in basis. Market 37.1M (was 17.2M), Europool pool 28.9M (was 13.0M), non-pool imports 8.2M (was 4.2M), wholesale 15.5M (was 9.2M), direct 21.6M (was 8.0M). The 27.9 / 28.0 / 26.3 / 18.0% channel shares used before are real published shares, but of the 31.74M sell-in and not of 17.2M, so applying them to 17.2M understated every channel by about 45%. The flow now has five channels: foreign online sellers are a new box.

What the 17.2M is (checked on Journal de l'Automobile and J2R, March 2025): the Syndicat du Pneu/GfK reports 17.211M TC4 tyres (cars, 4x4/SUV and vans) sold 'des revendeurs aux utilisateurs' (sell-out, +3.4%) and 31.744M sold 'des manufacturiers aux revendeurs' (sell-in, +4.5%); pure players sold about 5.6M (+21.9%). The research reads the 17.2M as the sell-out of two panelled channels only, auto-centres (8.86M) plus pneumaticiens (8.35M) = 17.21M, leaving out French pure players (5.68M, reported separately), dealers and independent repairers (MRA) and foreign e-tailers. I could not find the Syndicat's wording on panel scope or the 8.86M and 8.35M in the pages I could open. The check I could make is that the earlier file's channel shares of 27.9% and 26.3% (not re-checked) of 31.744M also give 17.2M. The research adds that 2025 fits the same reading (8.861M + 7.887M = 16.748M against 16.747M published; not checked).

Scope changes between years (research, partly checked): J2R reports 21.5M TC4 tyres sold in 2023 (-1.4%) and Journal de l'Automobile reports 16.493M of sell-out and 31.625M of sell-in for 2022 (February 2023), so the headline basis has changed more than once. The research reads the 2023 figure (21.3M in its version) as including pure players, the 2024 headline as excluding them, and the H1 2026 sell-out of 9.99M as including them again (not checked). Check the scope before comparing years. H1 2026: TC4 volumes were down 0.2% (J2R, 29 September 2026, checked); the research puts Europool sell-in at 14.6M.

Bridge for 2024 (research, million tyres, TC4 / passenger car): panel sell-out of auto-centres and pneumaticiens 17.21 / about 15.5, plus French pure players 5.68 / 5.1 = 22.89 / about 20.6 for all panelled channels, plus the Syndicat's residual for dealers and MRA 8.85 / 8.3 = Europool sell-in 31.74 / 28.9, plus non-pool imports 8.95 / 8.2 = total 40.7 / 37.1. For 2025 the research's central case is 40.0M TC4 and 36.4M passenger car (range 34.6-38.4M), with Europool sell-in of 30.58M (-4.4%), panel sell-out of 16.75M plus 5.09M of pure players (-10.3%) and a residual of about 8.74M. None of the 2025 figures is checked.

Wholesale versus direct is not published for France. The research's reconciled flows (low confidence): wholesale about 15.5M, of which about 9.0M pool and 6.5M non-pool; direct about 21.6M, of which 19.9M pool and about 1.7M non-pool. The model has no imports-to-direct flow, so it shows all 8.2M of non-pool supply through wholesale and the whole 21.6M as the direct box; pool to wholesale therefore reads 7.3M, and the wholesale and direct totals are the research's. The earlier file had 5.0M of pool plus 4.2M of imports through wholesale (9.2M, 54%) and 8.0M direct (46%).

Wholesalers (research; J2R checked): Distri Cash is the research's number one French tyre wholesaler and was missing from the earlier model. J2R (9 January 2024, checked) reports 5.5M tyres sold in 2022, revenue of EUR 480M in 2022, about EUR 550M expected for 2023 and 27 locations. Not found: the research's EUR 600M group revenue for 2024 (+20%, including parts), 10,000 clients, 715+ staff, 11+ agencies in about 85 départements (which conflicts with J2R's 27 locations), a 10% market share, a 3.5M-tyre figure and the statutory EUR 430.3M for Distri Cash Accessoires (Pappers, per the research). The research proposes 4-5M TC4 for Distri Cash, below the 5.5M J2R reported for 2022 (all tyre types, probably); the earlier file said about 6.5M for 2024. DPI (Doumerc Pneus) shows revenue of only about EUR 4.3M (research), so it is probably not a major wholesaler. Groupe Massa (1001pneus) and Alzura Tyres (ex-Tyre24) are named by the research as relevant; AAG, Autodis, Copadex, Chrono SLPA, PHE and Mobivia's Exadis are named only.

Retail and network players (research; no player publishes French tyre units, so every volume is an estimate scaled so that each channel sums to its panel-measured total). Checked: Feu Vert was acquired by Bassac, which completed the purchase of 100% of the holding company Financière Ramsès I SAS from Alpha Private Equity on 24 February 2026 (fusacq), with revenue of EUR 663M for the year to September 2025; the research's 350 centres (167 owned, 183 franchised), EUR 935M under the banner and PDG Thierry Sinquin staying were not found. Euromaster: ac-franchise (25 August 2026) says more than 470 centres, 222 of them franchised, with 250 targeted by 2027; the research says 485 centres (235 franchised) plus 1,100 mobile units, EUR 632.4M of revenue in 2024 and a net loss of EUR 2.1M, which I could not find. Midas: Mavis's June 2025 purchase of Midas from TBC covers about 1,200 locations in the United States and Canada, and the release does not mention Europe or France (checked); the research says Midas France has been Mobivia's since 2004 (not checked), which corrects the earlier note that Mavis bought Midas International. Siligom joined the FleetPartner alliance (BestDrive, Eurotyre, Feu Vert; 950 points of sale with Siligom, over 200 of them Siligom's) on 1 January 2024 (ac-franchise, checked); the research says Viasso is now Point S only, which I could not find stated. Allopneus: owned by Michelin (Auto Infos, checked); the 3.4M tyres, EUR 307M of revenue and 'près de 10%' share were not found; Auto Infos mentions an alliance with Feu Vert. Not checked: Speedy about 1.0-1.2M (4.5% share and over 1M tyres in 2016, EUR 281M in 2018), Norauto 410 centres, Point S 660, First Stop 330-350 centres, Côté Route (Bridgestone, Eurofleet), Eurotyre over 230, BestDrive about 210 (100% franchise), 1001pneus (Groupe Massa, 0.8M tyres in 6 countries). Not verified even by the research: Roady, L'Auto E.Leclerc, Profil Plus, Vulco, PRODY and 'Pneuwyz', so the 'Pneuwyz' entry is replaced by 1001pneus.

Structure corrections (research): the Eurogom group no longer exists as a structure (it split in 2015), so Siligom, Eurotyre and Côté Route are shown separately. Côté Route belongs to Bridgestone (Eurofleet), not to Eurogom. Eurofleet is Speedy, First Stop and Côté Route (about 900 centres); FleetPartner is BestDrive, Eurotyre, Feu Vert (leasing only) and Siligom (about 950 points of sale); Viasso is Point S. Euromaster is shown with 470-485 centres, not about 650.

Private versus commercial is about 78% / 22% (private 7.6 + 11.2 + 3.2 + 4.7 + 2.3 = 29.0M; commercial 1.0 + 2.8 + 3.7 + 0.4 + 0.2 = 8.1M). Only the pneumaticien figure has any evidence: GfK data cited by the Syndicat du Pneu say about 4M of roughly 25M car tyres in 2023 were sold B2B by pneumaticiens (research, not checked). Channel mixes are estimates.

Season mix and prices: J2R (checked) reports 2024 sales of summer 53%, all-season 37% (+19.2%) and winter 10%, with an average TC4 price of EUR 113 including VAT, and premium 50%, quality 21.5% and budget 19.1% of the market. Journal de l'Automobile attributes the 53 / 37 / 10 split to SUV tyres, so the scope is not certain; the research reads it as panel tourisme. Research, not checked: all-season reached 42% in 2025 (summer 49%, winter 9%), overtook summer in the second half of 2025 and reached 46% in the first half of 2026 (summer 49%, winter 5%); B-brands fell 16.5% in H1 2025 and 6.7% in H1 2026 while tradebrands grew; H1 2026 prices were EUR 101 for B-brands, EUR 89.20 for tradebrands and EUR 64.60 for budget.

Trade policy (checked on Sicurauto): Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1540, published 7 July 2026 and in force from 8 July with no retroactive effect, sets definitive anti-dumping duties on Chinese passenger-car and light-truck tyres from 4.3% (Hankook's Chinese entities) to 45.3% (residual rate), for five years, with 24.4% for the cooperating producers. The research adds that a parallel anti-subsidy case is due in December 2026 (not checked).

Trade data, kept from the earlier file: UN Comtrade / WITS 2024, HS 401110, as quoted by the research: France gross imports about 55.1M and exports about 20.2M passenger tyres. Not usable for the import and export boxes, because gross customs flows include OE supply and intra-group movements. Not checked here. The research also notes that Customs HS 401110 unit data for France were not obtained for the non-pool estimate.

Discrepancies the research asks us to carry: (1) the non-panel block is 8.3M passenger car on the Syndicat's convention but about 16.5M on the full-market basis, so either non-pool imports are below about 22% or dealers, MRA and foreign online are larger than the Syndicat assumes (ADEME's 2022 gap of about 25% and the 20% budget share support the larger figure; ADEME's scope may include retreads and used tyres, which would overstate it); (2) SUV tyres are about 10% of Europool sell-in but only 5.6% of panel sell-out volumes, which suggests they go disproportionately to dealers and online; (3) camionnette sell-in for 2024 is quoted at 2.0M by Zepros and 2.81M by L'argus and the Syndicat, and only 2.81M adds up to 31.74M; (4) Aliapur's collection figures (555 kt in 2024, 400 kt in 2025) are inconsistent, so ADEME tonnage (+6.2% in 2024) is used only as a growth cross-check.

Wholesale cross-check (October 2026): One name, Distri Cash, already covers about 35–42% of the 15.5M layer. That is enough to show the layer is not too high, but too little to test it. See the Wholesale check tab for the figures, sources and caveats.
flows.scope: Passenger-car replacement tyres (cars and 4x4/SUV, excludes vans; sell-in)

market.short: Pool sell-in 28.9M + estimated non-pool imports 8.2M. The pool part is published; the import part is an estimate.
how: The French trade body (Syndicat du Pneu, with GfK) reports that manufacturers sold 31.74M car, 4x4/SUV and van tyres to resellers in 2024. That is the Europool figure.
Taking the vans out (about 2.81M) leaves 28.9M for cars and 4x4/SUV.
Add the tyres that come from outside the pool, mostly Asian budget brands: the research estimates 8.2M (range 6.5–10.3M).
28.9M + 8.2M = 37.1M. Counting vans too, the same estimate is 40.7M.
The 17.2M used before was only the sell-out of two panelled channels, so it was not the whole market.
market.src: Research estimate built on published Europool sell-in (checked on J2R and Journal de l'Automobile).

sure.w: The 28.9M pool part is published and checked. The 8.2M of non-pool imports is the main uncertainty: it moves the market between about 35M and 39M.

market.why: The pool's sell-in is a hard number, but it leaves out budget brands that do not report to it, so the market would be understated. The research adds those as an estimate.
market.val: Sanity check: 37.1M ÷ 39.3M cars (SDES, 1 Jan 2024) = 0.94 tyres per car, high next to Germany (0.83) and Spain (0.80) in this dashboard. The pool alone is 0.74, so the 8.2M non-pool add-on is the part to challenge. The research also cites ADEME (42.2M light-vehicle tyres placed on the market in 2022, vans included) and a mileage model (39–48M), neither checked.

industry.short: Europool sell-in to French resellers: 31.74M including vans, 28.9M for cars and 4x4/SUV.
how: Europool sell-in to the French trade in 2024 was 31.744M tyres for cars, 4x4/SUV and vans, up 4.5%.
The research splits it as cars 25.64M + 4x4/SUV 3.29M + vans 2.81M (quoted from L'argus and the Syndicat, not checked).
Cars + 4x4/SUV = 28.9M. That is the figure used here; vans are left out.
Not every manufacturer reports to Europool. Non-EU, mostly Asian, suppliers are outside it.
industry.src: Syndicat du Pneu / GfK, via Journal de l'Automobile and J2R (checked).

sure.w: The 31.74M total is published and checked. The van deduction (2.81M) is quoted by the research and not checked.

industry.why: It is the only published count of what the main brands sold into France, so it is used as it is. Vans are taken out with the research's split by vehicle type, because this model covers cars and 4x4/SUV.
industry.val: Both sell-in quotes are kept with this figure. The split by type (cars 25.64M + 4x4/SUV 3.29M + vans 2.81M = 31.74M) is quoted by the research from L'argus and the Syndicat du Pneu, and was not checked.

import.short: About 22% of the market (8.2M) is assumed to come from outside the pool.
how: These are tyres from manufacturers that do not report to Europool, mostly Asian budget brands.

Support: budget brands were 19.1% of the 2024 market (J2R). The research also quotes a 2022 gap of about 25% between ADEME's 42.2M tyres placed on the market and Europool's 31.6M sell-in (not checked).
The research takes about 22% of the total (range 18–26%), which gives 8.2M.
The model has no flow for imports going straight to the channels, so all 8.2M is shown going through wholesale. About 1.7M of it really goes direct and sits in the Direct box instead.
import.src: Research estimate; the budget share is from J2R (checked).

sure.w: The main driver of the full-market figure, with a range of 6.5–10.3M.

import.why: Two separate hints point to about a fifth of the market being non-pool brands: budget brands' 19.1% share (J2R) and ADEME's gap of about 25% in 2022. The research settles on 22%.
import.val: The 19.1% budget share is in the quotes kept. The ADEME gap was not checked. Research range 6.5–10.3M. To challenge it: ask Apollo's French distributors what share of their volume is non-pool brands.

export.short: Set to zero. Re-exports exist but are not measured.
how: The research sees possible re-exports by French wholesalers (Distri Cash for example) of 0.3–1.0M, but they are not quantified.
ADEME counts the first company that places a tyre on the market, so its figures are not a clean net of exports.
The model sets export to 0.0M.

sure.w: A convention, not a measurement.

export.why: French wholesalers such as Distri Cash do re-export, but it is small and unmeasured, so zero is cleaner than guessing within the research's 0.3–1.0M.
export.val: Customs data (about 55.1M tyres imported and 20.2M exported in 2024, UN Comtrade as quoted, not checked) include factory flows and cannot be used for this box.

direct.short: About 58% of the market (21.6M) is assumed to reach the channels without a wholesaler.
how: No source publishes the wholesale / direct split for France.

The research estimates 19.9M of pool volume goes direct (manufacturer-owned networks such as Euromaster, Speedy, First Stop, BestDrive and Allopneus, and the central purchasing of auto-centres), plus about 1.7M of non-pool volume bought direct by networks and online sellers.
It adds up from the channels: 7.6 + 3.0 + 5.7 + 3.8 + 1.5 = 21.6M.

sure.w: Nothing published confirms the split.

direct.why: In France many fitting chains are owned or supplied by manufacturers (Euromaster, Speedy, First Stop, BestDrive, Allopneus) and the big auto-centres buy centrally, so a large part of the market skips wholesalers. Independent garages and dealers are the main wholesale customers.
direct.val: No source publishes it, and the research rates it low confidence. It shows how large manufacturer-owned networks are: Euromaster alone has more than 470 centres (ac-franchise, 25 Aug 2026). Best check: your own French sell-in by account type.

how: The pool's 28.9M minus the 21.6M that goes direct leaves 7.3M for wholesalers.

The research has 9.0M going from the pool to wholesalers. The difference, about 1.7M, is non-pool volume that goes direct. The model has no flow for that, so it counts it in the Direct box and the pool-to-wholesale figure reads lower.
toWs.src: Calculated from the industry and direct figures.

sure.w: Both inputs are estimates, and the model's one-flow simplification lowers it by about 1.7M versus the research.

toWs.why: In France many fitting chains are owned or supplied by manufacturers (Euromaster, Speedy, First Stop, BestDrive, Allopneus) and the big auto-centres buy centrally, so a large part of the market skips wholesalers. Independent garages and dealers are the main wholesale customers.
toWs.val: No source publishes it, and the research rates it low confidence. It shows how large manufacturer-owned networks are: Euromaster alone has more than 470 centres (ac-franchise, 25 Aug 2026). Best check: your own French sell-in by account type.

wsDom.short: Calculated: pool to wholesale + imports − exports.
how: Wholesalers sold 15.5M in France: 7.3M from the pool + 8.2M imports − 0.00M exports.
From the other side: market 37.1M − direct 21.6M = 15.5M. The two agree, so the flow closes.
wsDom.src: Calculated from the figures above. The research also reports about 15.5M via wholesale (9.0M pool + 6.5M non-pool).

sure.w: Built from estimates.

wsDom.val: Cross-check with the biggest wholesalers (October 2026): Distri Cash alone reported more than 5.5M tyres sold in 2022, 35–42% of these 15.5M. The other names publish no volumes, so this shows the layer is not too high but cannot test it.

ch.auto.tot.short: Panel sell-out of auto-centres (8.86M, TC4) × about 97% cars.
how: The Syndicat du Pneu / GfK panel covers auto-centres and fast-fitters (hypermarket auto-centres count here). The research quotes 8.86M TC4 tyres, 27.9% of the 31.74M sell-in (not checked).
About 97% of those are car tyres, the rest vans: 8.86M × 97% ≈ 8.6M.
ch.auto.tot.src: Syndicat du Pneu / GfK panel as quoted by the research (not checked).

sure.w: A measured panel figure, but quoted by the research and not checked.

ch.auto.tot.what: Auto-centres and fast-fitters such as Norauto, Midas, Feu Vert and Speedy, including hypermarket auto-centres.
ch.auto.tot.why: The Syndicat du Pneu/GfK panel measures what auto-centres sell, so this is the most solid channel number in the France model. Only the 97% car share is assumed.
ch.auto.tot.val: The panel headline is public (quote kept: 17.211M sell-out). The research's split into 8.86M for auto-centres and 8.35M for tyre specialists is not in the pages I could open.

ch.auto.ws.short: About 12% of this channel's tyres arrive via wholesalers (modelled).
how: Auto-centres & fast-fitters gets 8.6M tyres in total.
Assumed: about 12% of them (1.0M) arrive through wholesalers. Auto-centres buy mostly direct or through central purchasing.
The via-wholesale figures of all channels are set so they add up to the 15.5M that wholesalers sold in France, and the direct figures to 21.6M.
ch.auto.ws.src: No source publishes how each channel buys its tyres. This is a modelled split from the country research.

sure.w: A modelled split. Nothing published confirms it, so overwrite it if you know better.

ch.auto.ws.why: The research reasons network by network: auto-centres and manufacturer-led networks buy mostly direct (12–17% via wholesale), independent garages and dealers mainly through wholesalers such as Distri Cash (79%). The figures are then set so that all channels add up to 15.5M via wholesale and 21.6M direct.

meta.boxNote: No channel split is published for the UK, so the four channel totals are benchmark estimates. The import box is modelled non-pool supply, not customs imports, and export is a balancing item. Red and blue show where the tyre is physically stocked and delivered, so a tyre bought on a manufacturer contract but delivered by a distributor counts as via wholesale. Private and commercial are a car versus van mileage proxy, so read them as passenger and LCV. Finer boxes can be added in the editor.
meta.scopeNote: The card header's 28.4M is an older GfK/NTDA estimate; this model's 29.0M is an estimate from the number of cars on the road. The wholesale, direct, import and export figures are research estimates anchored on BTMA's H1 2024 EuroPool sales.
meta.walkNote: Red and blue show where the tyre is physically stocked and delivered, not who holds the contract. No UK channel split is published, so the four channel totals are benchmark shares. Private and commercial mean cars and vans.

channels.why: No UK channel split is published, so the four shares come from the German BRV split and the French panel, adjusted only for what Mintel says qualitatively: independents dominate, franchised dealers are losing share, online is growing.

refs: Method: no channel split is published for this country, so each channel share is a benchmark estimate anchored on the published German (BRV 2024: 71 / 20 / 3 / 6%) and French splits and adjusted for the country context noted below. Treat the shares as placeholders with an error of roughly +/-6 points until your team replaces them.

UK: independent garages dominate and fast-fit networks are stable or growing, while franchised dealers have been losing share (Mintel, qualitative; the numbers are paywalled). Online is a growing but smaller channel.
Market size: Estimate: 36.2M licensed cars (DfT, end-2024) x about 0.80 tyres per car per year. An older GfK/NTDA study put the market at 28.4M

BTMA/EuroPool: members sold 9.330M UK consumer replacement tyres (passenger car, SUV, light commercial) in H1 2024, as reported by European Rubber Journal. Doubled to 18.7M for the year; seasonality and stock timing are why the range is 18.2-19.3M. The research also quotes 4.786M for Q2 2024 (not checked).

Pool versus market: 29.0M less 18.7M leaves about 10.3M (35%) outside the EuroPool members. BTMA links member volumes to low-cost imports, particularly from China and Vietnam (European Rubber Journal). The research also quotes extra-EU passenger and light-truck imports up 10% in 2024 and well above 30M tyres a year, and GfK's 2023 UK mix of 33% premium, 22% mid-range and 45% budget. None of that was checked here, and customs imports cannot go in the import box because they include pool brands, OE supply and stock.

Wholesale structure: Micheldever supplies about 6.0M tyres a year (Sumitomo Rubber Industries agreed to buy it in January 2017). Stapleton's calls itself the UK's largest distributor, with 11 locations, and has been owned by Itochu since 1994. The research also cites more than 7,000 independent customers for Stapleton's and more than 6,000 retailers for Micheldever (not checked). Do not add these up: they include own retail and overlapping customers.

Halfords sold its Viking distribution business to Bond International in FY2024, expecting savings of about 5M GBP a year while keeping the margin benefits of direct sourcing (Tyrepress). It shows why direct versus wholesale is blurry: sourcing can be direct while stock and delivery run through a distributor.

Wholesale versus direct is an inference from market structure, about 72 / 28 with a range of 67-78% wholesale, not a reported percentage. Channel routing has the lowest confidence of all: specialists about 82% via wholesale, dealers 54%, other retail 75%, online 39%.

Ownership (research, not checked): Micheldever and Protyre belong to Sumitomo Rubber, Stapleton's and Kwik Fit sit within Itochu's European Tyre Enterprise, and Blackcircles is Michelin-owned. The large UK wholesalers are therefore not independent in the ownership sense.

Private versus commercial is a mileage proxy. The research quotes DfT 2024 Great Britain vehicle miles of 256.1bn for cars and taxis and 58.5bn for vans, which puts vans at about 18.6% of the total and about 5.4M of the 29.0M tyres. Not checked here.

Wholesale cross-check (October 2026): Micheldever and Bond together handle roughly 11.5–14.5M tyres, about 55–70% of the 21.0M layer. Part of that layer is manufacturer-owned. See the Wholesale check tab for the figures, sources and caveats.

market.source: Research estimate, medium confidence, built from RecyBEM data. The research projects about 10.25M tyres of all types placed on the Dutch market in 2026 (RecyBEM January-August 2026 6.45M against 6.22M a year earlier, +3.7%; newsletter figures quoted by the research, not checked; full year projected at the 2025 seasonality of 62.8% by August). Times 0.96 for the consumer scope (cars and SUV/4x4 about 80% plus vans and light trucks about 16%; caravan, trailer and other tyres, 4%, left out; the split is assumed) gives 9.84M, the same scope as ETRMA's PCT as you define it. 2024 actual for comparison: 9,990,534 placed (checked), 9.59M. The period differs a little from the ETRMA rolling year: a trailing 12 months to August 2026 would be about 10.13M x 0.96 = 9.72M, about 1% lower. About 0.85M of undeclared tyres (foreign webshops, tyres from scrapped cars) sit outside this figure, so total domestic demand is about 10.69M. Replaces the 2024 figure of 9.59M.

industry.source: ETRMA Pool Market Data (Europe excl. Turkey, by country, rolling year), supplied by you: Netherlands RY2026 9,406,575 tyres, against 9,465,749 in RY2025 (-0.6%); rounded to 9.41M. This is pool members' sell-in, so it is gross: it includes tyres invoiced to Dutch customers that are re-exported (see the Export box) and is not domestic sales. Scope: ETRMA PCT, which you confirm covers cars, SUV/4x4, vans and light trucks. To confirm: the screenshot header is cut off, so I read RY2026 as the 12 months to September 2026; and whether the table allocates volume by invoice-to or ship-to country. The research's own RecyBEM-based estimate of this figure was 9.00M for 2026 (8.54M for 2024); ETRMA is 0.41M higher, and that gap sits in the Export box at your instruction. Replaces the earlier 8.54M.

import.source: Research estimate, medium confidence, range plus or minus 0.3M: non-pool and parallel imports, same scope, 2026. RecyBEM 'import only' members (295 members, about 70% of the membership; checked) first-placed 2,954,121 tyres of all types in 2024 and 116 one-off declarants placed 19,712 (checked); times 0.96 that is 2.85M, and the research holds 2026 flat at 2.84M. The category overlaps: 'import only' volume includes pool brands bought abroad (parallel imports), and the regular method includes some non-pool imports by large wholesalers. The research sends about 0.42M of it straight to channels. The model has no imports-to-channel flow, so all 2.84M is shown going through wholesale and that volume sits in the direct box instead.

export.source: Estimate, not published: it closes the flow so that the boxes add up, ETRMA industry 9.41M + imports 2.84M - market 9.84M = 2.41M. It holds two parts that cannot be separated: about 2.0M that the research estimates for re-export by Dutch hubs in 2026 (2024: RecyBEM refunded the fee on 1,874,255 tyres of all types exported by 38 members, checked, which is 1.80M after x 0.96), and about 0.41M by which ETRMA's pool figure is above what RecyBEM's declarations imply (research 9.00M). You chose to place that gap here: pool tyres invoiced to Dutch customers and shipped abroad that RecyBEM never sees as refunded exports. If the gap really belongs in imports or in the Dutch market, export would be about 2.0M instead. The market is already net of export. Customs trade flows (see Sources and notes) are far larger and are not netted here.

direct.source: Research estimate, medium confidence, scaled from the research's 2026 car figure: 2.85M x 1.2 = 3.42M, being about 3.0M of pool volume sold direct plus 0.42M of non-pool imports bought direct by e-tailers and garages (2.50M and 0.35M for cars). The research gives no route split for vans and light trucks, so they are assumed to follow the car split. The model has no imports-to-channel flow, so the whole 3.42M is the direct box and the wholesale side receives all 2.84M of imports. 'Industry sold to wholesale' therefore reads 5.99M, which is 0.42M lower than ETRMA pool minus the research's direct pool volume (9.41M - 3.00M = 6.41M). Equals the sum of the channel direct figures. Replaces the 2024 figure of 3.30M.

meta.boxNote: Boxes are the channels as named under "By channel". Industry is ETRMA pool sell-in (9.41M, rolling year 2026), which is gross: it includes tyres invoiced to Dutch customers that are re-exported, so it does not compare directly with domestic sales. Export (2.41M) closes the flow: it is ETRMA industry plus imports minus the 9.84M market, and holds about 2.0M of re-export that the research estimates plus about 0.4M by which ETRMA is above what RecyBEM implies (your choice to place the gap here). The market is net of it. The import box is the 2.84M of non-pool and parallel imports, shown going through wholesale. The research sends about 0.42M of it straight to channels; the model has no such flow, so that volume sits in the direct box and 'industry sold to wholesale' (5.99M) reads 0.42M lower than ETRMA pool minus the direct pool volume (6.41M). The research gives the channel, wholesale versus direct and private versus commercial splits for cars only, so those figures are its 2026 car numbers multiplied by 1.2, which assumes vans and light trucks follow the car shares (vans lean commercial, so commercial is probably understated). Online is the seller of record and leaves out the undeclared foreign-webshop purchases (part of about 0.85M of undeclared leakage that also includes tyres from scrapped cars). Private and commercial are modelled from lease-fleet and mileage data, and the channel split is not published.
meta.scopeNote: Period: rolling year RY2026 (I read it as the 12 months to September 2026). Industry is ETRMA's Pool Market Data for the Netherlands, 9,406,575 tyres, supplied by you (RY2025 9,465,749, -0.6%); it covers cars, SUV/4x4, vans and light trucks together (ETRMA PCT). The market (9.84M) is the research's 2026 projection of RecyBEM placements (about 10.25M tyres of all types) times 0.96 for the same consumer scope, leaving out caravan, trailer and other tyres; the 80 / 16 / 4 split between cars and SUV/4x4, vans and light trucks, and other is an assumption, because RecyBEM does not publish placements by tyre type. About 0.85M consumer tyres that RecyBEM does not see (foreign webshops, tyres from scrapped cars) sit outside it, so total domestic demand is about 10.69M. Everything below the industry figure is modelled, not published. For comparison, the 2024 version of this flow had industry 8.54M (a research estimate from RecyBEM declarations), market 9.59M, imports 2.85M and export 1.80M.

refs: Scope and method (rebuilt October 2026): the Netherlands flow now covers cars, SUV/4x4, vans and light trucks together as passenger-car replacement, which is ETRMA's PCT scope, on a 2026 rolling-year basis (RY2026). The industry box is ETRMA's own Pool Market Data for the Netherlands (9,406,575 tyres in RY2026), supplied by you. The supply side below it comes from the research (RecyBEM data) for 2026 in the same consumer scope: market 9.84M, non-pool and parallel imports 2.84M and domestic pool about 7.00M. Export (2.41M) is the balancing figure: ETRMA 9.41 + imports 2.84 - market 9.84. The research gives the channel, wholesale versus direct and private versus commercial splits for cars only, so those are its 2026 car figures multiplied by 1.2 (cars are 83.3% of the consumer scope: 8.2M cars x 1.2 = 9.84M). That assumes vans and light trucks follow the same channel and route shares as cars. Vans lean commercial, so the commercial share (24%, from the car data) is probably understated. Caravan, trailer and other tyres (4% of RecyBEM placements, an assumption) stay out. No Dutch source publishes sell-out by these channels or supply routes, so everything below the industry figure is an estimate. Earlier versions of this flow: cars only for 2024 (market 8.0M, industry 7.12M), then consumer scope for 2024 (market 9.59M, industry 8.54M, a research estimate from RecyBEM declarations).

How ETRMA's figure fits the RecyBEM data (October 2026): your ETRMA Pool table shows 9,406,575 tyres for the Netherlands in RY2026 and 9,465,749 in RY2025 (-0.6%). The research's own estimate of the same layer, built from RecyBEM declarations, is lower: 9.00M for 2026 and 8.54M for 2024, so ETRMA is about 0.4M higher on the 2026 basis (and RY2025 is about 0.9M above the 2024 estimate). Bridge in million tyres: ETRMA gross pool 9.41 = domestic pool 7.00 + re-export 2.41; domestic pool 7.00 + non-pool and parallel imports 2.84 = 9.84 market. The domestic pool of 7.00M is the research's figure and is not changed, so the extra 0.41M sits in Export, which you chose as the place to absorb the gap (the alternatives were the Dutch market, which would rise to about 10.25M, or imports, which would fall to about 2.43M). The direction differs too: ETRMA is down 0.6% while RecyBEM placements (all brands) are up 3.7% in January-August 2026 (newsletter figures quoted by the research, not checked), which suggests that non-pool volume or hub re-export is gaining against pool-member sell-in. The research's assumption of 5% pool growth to 2026 is not supported by ETRMA and is no longer used. The research found that the 9M figure fits only as gross pool sell-in that includes hub re-exports, and rejected it as domestic pool. Still to confirm: the month in which RY2026 ends (I assume September 2026), whether ETRMA allocates volume by invoice-to or ship-to country, and the exact category definition of the table.

The market in the model is the research's 2026 projection (9.84M = about 10.25M x 0.96); what follows is the data trail behind it. Market size (checked on RecyBEM's AVV-monitor autobanden 2024, dated 31 July 2025, figures as of 22 July 2025 and open to correction): 11,864,789 tyres declared, of which 1,874,255 were exported with restitution (38 exporting members), leaving 9,990,534 placed on the Dutch market (9,970,822 by members and 19,712 by 116 one-off declarants). 295 members used the 'import only' declaration (about 70% of the membership) and placed 2,954,121 tyres; that leaves regular-method gross of 8,890,956 and net of 7,016,701 (arithmetic checked). The report lists 'Gegevens ETRMA' among the controls the environment inspectorate (ILT) described for checking declarations, but does not say how the data is used, so the research's step that regular declarations match pool sell-in is its own inference. RecyBEM expects the final 2024 figure to reach at least 10.9M (all types; times 0.96 about 10.46M, which the research reads as 9.59M declared plus 0.85M undeclared leakage). Later figures are from RecyBEM newsletters quoted by the research and not checked: about 9.9M placed and 10.4M collected in 2025, and 6.45M placed (6.94M collected) in January-August 2026 against 6.22M a year earlier (+3.7%), which the research projects to about 10.25M for 2026 using the 62.8% January-August share of 2025. The research notes that RecyBEM's 2025 newsletters are internally inconsistent (December 2025 swaps 8.5M placed and 8M collected; January 2026 gives the same 8.0M to end-November as to end-October) and treats the February 2026 full-year figure as authoritative. The 80 / 16 / 4 scope split is assumed.

Parc, mileage and lease fleet: the Dutch passenger-car parc was just over 9.4M cars on 1 January 2026, 1.8% more than a year earlier, 87.7% (nearly 8.3M) registered to private owners (CBS, checked). VNA's Autoleasemarkt in cijfers 2025 (checked) shows 873,500 business-lease cars (+1.6%), 241,800 private-lease cars (-2.5%), 256,600 lease vans and 1,371,900 in total at end-2025 (859,700, 247,900 and 260,400 at end-2024). Cars returned at contract end averaged 25,100 km a year (business lease) and 13,300 km (private lease) in 2025 (VNA, checked); privately owned cars drove about 11,100 km in 2024 (CBS, checked earlier). On that basis lease cars are about 21-22% of car kilometres, and with the seasonal two-set fitments the research puts commercial demand at about 24% of passenger-car tyres. That 24% is a car figure and is applied here to the whole consumer scope; lease vans (256,600) and other commercial vans and light trucks are not in it, so commercial demand is probably higher. Not published by channel.

Customs versus domestic balance: gross trade is large and sources disagree, none of it checked. UN Comtrade (quoted in the earlier research) shows 31.746M passenger-car tyres (HS 401110) imported and 21.160M exported in 2024. The research quotes WITS at 21.36M exported in 2023 and IndexBox at 17M exported in 2025, down 33.8%, which implies about 25.7M in 2024 (the research's own arithmetic). These flows include manufacturer distribution centres and re-export, so they describe a European hub and are much larger than the 1.8M re-export layer, which is the part RecyBEM refunded. They are not netted against domestic sales.

Wholesale versus direct is a modelled split, not a published figure. The research's reconciled 2026 flows, cars only (built on a 9.0M pool): pool gross 7.50M, re-export 1.65M, domestic pool 5.85M (3.35M to wholesale, 2.50M direct) plus non-pool and parallel imports 2.35M (2.00M to wholesale, 0.35M direct) make 8.2M, with wholesale 5.35M and direct 2.85M (65 / 35). Multiplied by 1.2 for the consumer scope: domestic pool 7.00M (about 4.0M to wholesale, 3.0M direct) plus imports 2.84M (about 2.4M to wholesale, 0.4M direct) make 9.84M, with wholesale 6.42M and direct 3.42M. With ETRMA at 9.41M, re-export becomes 2.41M instead of the research's 2.0M and the domestic pool is unchanged. The model has no imports-to-channel flow, so it shows all 2.84M of imports through wholesale and 3.42M as the direct box; 'industry sold to wholesale' therefore reads 5.99M, not the 6.41M of pool that is not sold direct. The pool and import split is a range of plus or minus 0.3M, because 'import only' volume includes pool brands bought abroad. The research quotes the ACM's 2021 merger decision as saying most tyres are sold via wholesalers; I did not find that sentence on the ACM summary page.

Wholesale layer (2026 basis; the research's car ranges multiplied by 1.2 for this scope, wholesale node about 6.4M; volume passed from one wholesaler to another is not added twice): Global Automotive Investments Holding about 60% of the node, 3.5-4.3M domestic (research range for cars 2.9-3.6M, which the research cut from an earlier 3.3-4.0M because the node is smaller than assumed and Fource volume must not be counted twice). The research bases this on EW Top 500 revenue of EUR 1.93bn (2025 edition) and EUR 1.8bn (2023), mostly exports and other EU countries (not checked). Inter-Sprint 1.1-1.6M, including volume to Fource (stock quoted at 2.7-3.8M tyres depending on the source, hundreds of containers a month go abroad; I could not confirm current figures). Banden Express with Reedijk 1.2-1.6M (12 depots, deliveries 3 times a day, 100+ vans; not checked). Van den Ban 0.48-0.84M, mostly export (139 employees per Tracxn, July 2026; revenue figures of unclear scope). PBG / Mega Tyre 0.36-0.60M. LKQ Fource and Autobandenpartner 0.36-0.60M is pass-through inside Global Automotive and is not added. Alliance Automotive Benelux with Tyfoon 0.12-0.36M, largely Tyfoon private label imported. Other wholesalers and importers 1.8-2.6M is the remainder (derived, low confidence). Heuver's own site presents it as a B2B wholesaler for truck, agricultural and earthmoving tyres and does not mention passenger-car tyres, so it is not shown as a passenger-car wholesaler. The 1.2 multiplier assumes vans and light trucks move through the same wholesalers as cars.

Global Automotive Investments Holding (checked on the ACM decision of 10 March 2021 and Tyrepress): the group's operating companies are Inter-Sprint, Van den Ban Autobanden, Tyreteam, Banden Express, Reedijk Banden Import, Inter Tyre Holland and Wheel Tyre, and the ACM cleared its purchase of PBG (Pon Banden Groep, with Mega Tyre and Summa) from Pon Holdings that year. Its Dutch share of wholesale is a share-of-node estimate with no company accounts behind it: the 2023-2025 KvK accounts were filed but sit behind a paywall and were not reviewed, and group revenue covers the whole group across Europe, so it is not a Dutch volume.

Retail and online players (2026 basis, the research's car ranges multiplied by 1.2): no player publishes Dutch unit volumes, so every figure is a research estimate (outlets times an assumed throughput, or a share of the channel) with low to medium confidence. Kwik Fit 0.84-1.2M (165 outlets on kwik-fit.nl; Autointernationaal, 6 Sept 2026, says 160 today and BNR, 7 Sept 2026, has director Paul Traas planning growth by almost 10% to 175; both checked, and the research notes the conflict between the website figure and the 160). Profile and Distri24 0.54-0.90M ('more than 200 outlets in Belgium and the Netherlands' including truck sites per the research, about 170 in the Netherlands; not checked). Euromaster 0.42-0.72M, about 65% commercial (80 own plus 26 partner locations in March 2025 and about 120,000 lease wheel swaps a year; not checked). Bosch Car Service 0.36-0.60M (no new data). Autobandenpartner garages 0.30-0.54M of fitted volume, the same tyres as Fource's sell-in. AutoCrew 0.06-0.18M. Online: Delticom Netherlands 0.18-0.36M, which the research places under autobandenmarkt.nl, banden-giga.nl, bandenprijzen24.nl and probanden.nl (not ReifenDirekt.nl; the shop list is not checked), part of which may sit in the foreign-webshop layer. Delticom group revenue was EUR 484M in 2025 (EUR 482M in 2024) and GMV EUR 601M (EUR 597M), with 2026 guidance of EUR 480-520M (annual report, checked; the release names no countries, so the Netherlands is not disclosed). The research adds Q1 2026 revenue of EUR 99M (-6.1%), not checked. BandenConcurrent 0.18-0.36M (all-season 62.4% of its sales per the research, not checked). Dealers: no group-level volumes were found.

Latest signals: Tyres Europe (checked) reports European consumer replacement sell-in up 3% in Q2 2026 to 51.987M and up 2% in H1 to 110.133M; all-season was up 15% in Q2 and 9% in H1, summer down 1% and winter down 5%. Its Q1 2026 figure was 58.144M units against 57.499M (+1%; research, not checked); the research flags a typo in the Tyres Europe news index ('Q2 2026 vs Q1 2025, +1%'). EU27 and UK imports of passenger and light-truck tyres were down 6% to 67M units in January-May 2026, with China down 24% to 39M and its share falling from 72% to 58% (Tyres Europe, checked). The EU's definitive anti-dumping duties on Chinese passenger-car and light-truck tyres (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1540, dated 6 July 2026, in force 8 July, checked) range from 4.3% to 45.3%, with 24.4% for the other cooperating Chinese producers (checked on Sicurauto); China supplied nearly 93M units, 28% of the EU market, in 2024 (checked). BOVAG's August 2025 sample found almost 39% of cars on all-season tyres, a fleet fitment share and not a replacement sales mix. RecyBEM notes that private purchases from foreign online sellers can fall outside the Dutch placement statistics.

Caveats from the research: the 80 / 16 / 4 scope split and the 0.96 consumer factor are assumed, so every figure carries that uncertainty; the market is a calendar-2026 projection while ETRMA is a rolling year, a difference of about 1%; the channel, route and private versus commercial splits are car figures scaled by 1.2 (see the first note); the pool and import categories overlap; group figures such as Global Automotive's revenue are not Dutch volumes; and the research did not find RecyBEM's AVV-monitor for 2025, so it suggests asking RecyBEM or Band & Milieu for the 2025 split by declaration method. For Vredestein the research recommends tagging its own invoices by ship-to country (to get its own re-export ratio against the market-wide figure: 2.41 / 9.41 = 26% on the RY2026 basis here, or 22% on RecyBEM's 2024 data alone), using RecyBEM's monthly Bandenbalans as the domestic check, and treating the 60% concentration at Global Automotive as a key-account risk.

Wholesale cross-check (October 2026): Company data cannot test the 6.42M domestic figure. It does hint that Dutch wholesalers move more tyres across the border than the model's 2.84M in and 2.41M out. See the Wholesale check tab for the figures, sources and caveats.

market.short: RecyBEM's 2026 projection for consumer tyres: about 10.25M tyres × 0.96.
how: RecyBEM, the Dutch tyre-recycling scheme, records every tyre placed on the Dutch market. For 2024 it shows 9,990,534 tyres net of exports, all types.
For 2026 the research projects about 10.25M tyres of all types, based on RecyBEM's January–August 2026 figures (6.45M against 6.22M a year earlier, +3.7%; newsletter figures, not checked).
× 0.96 keeps only consumer tyres (cars, SUV/4x4, vans, light trucks) and drops caravan, trailer and other tyres: 9.84M. The 96% is an assumption.
About 0.85M more consumer tyres that RecyBEM does not see (foreign webshops, tyres from scrapped cars) are not in this figure.
market.src: Research estimate built on RecyBEM data (the 2024 figure was checked in the RecyBEM report).

sure.w: The 2024 actual is published and checked; 2026 is a projection, and the 96% consumer share is assumed. Its period (calendar 2026) differs slightly from the ETRMA rolling year.

market.why: RecyBEM is the closest thing to a full count of tyres placed on the Dutch market, because its members declare them. The 2026 level is projected from this year's trend, and a 96% factor keeps only consumer tyres.
market.val: The 2024 actual is published (quote kept: 9,990,534 tyres, all types). Sanity check: 9.84M ÷ 9.4M cars (CBS, 1 Jan 2026) = 1.05 tyres per car, the highest in this dashboard. Vans and light trucks are in the 9.84M but not in the car count, so the like-for-like figure is lower.

It is the pool members' sell-in for cars, SUV/4x4, vans and light trucks together (ETRMA PCT, as you confirmed).
It is gross: it includes tyres invoiced to Dutch customers and shipped abroad, so it is not Dutch domestic sales.
Rounded to 9.41M. The research's own RecyBEM-based estimate was 9.00M; the 0.41M difference sits in the Export box, at your instruction.

export.short: The balancing figure that closes the flow: 9.41 + 2.84 − 9.84.
how: Export closes the flow: industry 9.41M + imports 2.84M − market 9.84M = 2.41M.

It holds two parts that cannot be separated. About 2.0M is re-export by Dutch hubs, which the research estimates (in 2024 RecyBEM refunded the fee on 1,874,255 tyres of all types exported by 38 members, which is 1.80M after × 0.96).
The other 0.41M is the amount by which ETRMA is above what RecyBEM implies (the research's 9.00M). You asked to place that gap here.
If the gap really belongs in imports or in the Dutch market, export would be about 2.0M instead.
export.src: A balancing figure, not published. The 2024 re-export figure is from RecyBEM (checked).

sure.w: A balancing figure. Customs trade flows are far larger and are not netted here.

export.why: Dutch hubs re-export a lot, so something has to absorb the gap between ETRMA's gross pool sales plus imports and the Dutch market. export.val: RecyBEM refunded the fee on 1,874,255 exported tyres in 2024 (1.80M for consumer scope; quote kept), the same order of magnitude as the 2.0M. The 0.41M cannot be checked: if it really belongs in imports or in the Dutch market, export would be about 2.0M.

meta.boxNote: Boxes are the channels as named under "By channel". The import box is net non-pool supply, the 6.3M gap between the 21.06M market and the Europool pool, not gross imports (Asian consumer-tyre imports alone were about 13.4M, and they include pool brands made in Asia). The research sends 0.50M of the non-pool volume straight to channels (online pure players and autocentro private labels). The model has no such flow, so the whole 6.3M is shown going through wholesale and that 0.50M sits in the direct box instead; pool to wholesale therefore reads 8.4M, not the research's 8.9M. Export is set to zero because the MITECO figure is already net of exports; the research sees 0.2-0.5M of Europool volume as possibly re-exported. Online is the seller of record, so orders fitted at a workshop sit in the online box. Private and commercial are a planning assumption only.
meta.scopeNote: The market size is the MITECO producer register total as analysed by ADINE: 17.934M passenger-car plus 3.125M van, 4x4 and SUV new replacement tyres. The research recommends the 21.06M consumer total as the headline because MITECO's passenger-car line is not like-for-like with Europool's (SUV-fitment tyres sit partly in 'turismo'). A passenger-car-only cut of 17.93M is a secondary view and is not in the flow. Everything below the market and Europool figures is modelled: about 6.3M (30%) of the market sits outside the Europool pool.
meta.walkNote: Only the market (the ministry register) and the Europool figure are published. Everything below is modelled. The register and Europool do not classify tyres in exactly the same way, so the 6.3M non-pool gap is partly a classification difference. The model has no flow for imports going straight to channels, so “industry sold to wholesale” reads 8.4M, not the research's 8.9M.

channels.why: The research's reconciled 2024 flow: specialists, fast-fit and garages 82%, dealers 9.5%, other retail 2.4%, online 6.2%. It is built from GiPA/Ganvam workshop shares and GfK panel shares.
