refs: Method (replaced with the newest Spain research file, October 2026): the supply flows, channel totals, wholesale versus direct split and private versus commercial split now follow the research's reconciled 2024 flow, version 1 (passenger car, van and 4x4/SUV together, the research's recommended headline): specialists, fast-fit and garages 17.26M, dealers 2.00M, other retail 0.50M, online 1.30M, 21.06M in total, replacing the earlier 80 / 9.5 / 3 / 7.5% shares. Only the market and Europool totals are published; everything below them is an estimate. The research's passenger-car-only version 2 (MITECO turismo, 17.93M) is a secondary cut and is not in the flow.

Market size (checked on ADINE's release as reported by Posventa, and on the MITECO PDF 'Sistema de información de neumáticos 2024'): 24,559,740 new replacement tyres and 291,098 t in 2024, +9.6% (+2,142,129 on 22,417,611 in 2023). By segment: passenger car 17,934,194 (73%), van/4x4/SUV 3,124,549 (12.7%), truck and bus 1,532,446, moto 1,325,375, agricultural 231,135, public works and industrial 112,775, handling, quad and other 299,266. The data come from the producer register, tyre section, and cover new tyres placed on the replacement market by producers, importers and intra-EU acquirers adhered to SIGNUS and TNU, not original equipment; used (170,692) and retreaded (134,729) tyres are declared separately in the PDF. The PDF's own category unit rows, as I could read them, differ from ADINE's (passenger car 15,191,656, van/4x4/SUV 3,679,718, truck and bus 1,475,253, moto 1,300,694) and add up to 22.2M, not to its 24,559,740 total, while its tonnes add up. I used ADINE's split, which adds up exactly. The reporting deadline for 2025 data is 31 March 2026 on Posventa and 2 April 2026 in the research. MITECO's 2025 data are not yet published in the sources found.

Passenger car versus consumer (research; the Europneus split is not checked): Europool's 2024 consumer split was turismo about 11.6M (flat), 4x4-SUV 1.9M (+12%) and van about 1.1M (+7%). MITECO's 'camionetas, 4x4, todoterreno y SUV' line is 3.12M tyres at an average of 12.4 kg (38,744 t), against 7.6 kg for turismo (136,300 t), both derived from tonnes. If both sources used the same definitions, non-pool van/4x4/SUV would be only about 0.12M, which is implausible next to Asian consumer imports of 13.4M. The research concludes that MITECO's van/4x4/SUV line holds heavier LT-type and large 4x4 tyres, while many SUV-fitment tyres are declared as turismo, especially by importers. The two classifications are therefore not like-for-like, which is why the model headlines the 21.06M consumer total.

Pool versus market: Europool consumer sell-in of 14.775M (+2%) is quoted by the research from Europneus and I could not find it online. 21.059M less 14.775M leaves 6.284M (about 30%) of non-pool supply, which is the import box here; it is derived, not published. The research notes a conflicting claim that import brands are 'cuatro de cada diez' tyres sold (Goodyear Spain's head of consumer sales, via Europneus, on a sell-out basis; not checked) and suggests showing 40% as an upper sensitivity. Asian consumer-tyre imports were 13,445,760 units in 2024 (+17.1%, ADINE via the research, not checked) but include Asian-made pool-brand tyres, so they cannot stand in for non-pool supply.

The growth signals conflict (research): consumer growth in 2024 was +9% on MITECO (from over 19.3M in 2023), +10.1% on ADINE's Distripool (checked on Europneus and Interempresas: passenger car +9.7%, van +5.6%, 4x4/SUV +16.1%, second half +12.3%), +2% for Europool, +3.1% for GfK sell-out (11,215,604 units and EUR 1,138.9M, about EUR 101.5 a tyre; not checked) and +2.8% for OPEN specialist networks (not checked). The research reads this as growth through wholesalers' non-pool imports plus channel stock-building of 0.5-1.0M (estimate), with end-consumer demand up about 3%, so 2024 sell-out should not be taken as equal to sell-in. The research calls Distripool PwC-audited with over 70% of distribution; the pages I checked say only that it was prepared with PwC's consultancy and give no coverage figure.

Wholesale versus direct is not published for Spain. The research's reconciled flows (low confidence): Europool's 14.78M splits 8.90M to wholesale and 5.88M direct; the 6.28M of non-pool supply splits 5.78M to wholesale and 0.50M direct (online pure players and autocentro private labels that import as producers). That gives wholesale 14.68M (70%) and direct 6.38M (30%). The model has no imports-to-direct flow, so it shows all 6.28M of non-pool supply through wholesale and the whole 6.38M as the direct box; pool to wholesale therefore reads 8.40M (the research has 8.90M), and the wholesale and direct totals are the research's. The earlier file had 8.87M of pool plus the whole 6.28M through wholesale (15.15M, 72%) and 5.91M direct (28%).

Channels (research; the GfK and GiPA figures are as quoted and not checked): GiPA/Ganvam attribute 88% of tyre changes to specialists (37%), independent mechanics (40%) and autocentros (11%); GfK puts specialists at 47% and autocentros at 13.4% of panel volume; the research sets the combined workshop channel at 82% after allowing for tyres bought online and fitted there. Dealers are 9.5% on GfK's 'talleres oficiales'. The research flags a shift in 2026: specialists fell to 43.0% of GfK volume to May 2026 from 46.1% a year earlier, towards autocentros, general garages and online.

Wholesale scale: wholesalers publish revenue, not tyre units, so the card ranks them on group revenue (it includes retail, truck, moto, agricultural and export sales). Checked: Grupo Soledad EUR 409M consolidated in 2024 (+1.6%) and Neumáticos Soledad SL EUR 355.96M (+1.63%), both Alicante Plaza. Not checked (research, from Infocap's Ruta del Neumático 2025-2026 and company sites): Soledad EUR 406.8M and rank 1, EUR 323.92M national, 18 logistics centres; Grupo Andrés EUR 385M group and about EUR 360M from tyres (rank 2 and largest pure distributor), 4.0M tyres of all types in 2023, 5 warehouses, more than 1M tyres in stock, 57 countries; NEX EUR 290.4M (+13.8%), 3.6M tyres (year not stated), 25 warehouses; Top Recambios EUR 238.4M in 2023 (EUR 260.6M in another ranking); Recacor EUR 131.5M (estimate); Grupo Total Neumáticos EUR 43.4M in 2023. Infocap's top 50 distributors total EUR 2,135.9M (+5.4%), and only 20 of the 50 are pure distributors. These figures overlap and must not be added up. The earlier file said NEX sold more than 2.5M tyres in 2024; the research now quotes 3.6M from the company site with no year.

NEX (checked on Tyrepress, December 2014): Nex Tyres SL was set up as a 50 / 50 wholesale partnership of Euromaster Automoción y Servicios and Rodi Metro for car and light-commercial-vehicle tyres, trading from 2015. The research adds that the CNMC authorised it in 2015 and that Rodi bought back Michelin's 20% stake in Rodi in January 2026, with Michelin and Rodi keeping their shareholding links in NEX (not checked). It supplies the Euromaster and Rodi networks and independents, so it is Michelin-linked, not independent.

Retail and network players (research, mostly not checked; no player publishes Spanish tyre units, so volumes are derived from revenue): Euromaster España has 443 workshops in Spain and 540 in Iberia and reported revenue of EUR 430M in 2024 (+8%, Motor16, checked; the article does not say whether this is Spain only, and Iberia is above EUR 508M), with 'more than 6%' of light-vehicle tyres, which would be only about 1.26M tyres. The research's 1.6M comes from a 2025 company release of more than 1.7M light-vehicle tyres (+7%, not checked). Rodi: 180+ outlets, EUR 307.8M in 2025 and about EUR 278M in 2024, est. 0.7-1.0M tyres including truck. Norauto: 91 autocentros, EUR 243.5M, est. 0.7M; Feu Vert: 95-105 outlets, EUR 139.0M, est. 0.4M (both assume about 30% of revenue is tyres at EUR 101.5 a tyre; low confidence). Aurgi and Motortown: 62 + 48 outlets, EUR 71.4M (probably 2023). First Stop: 607 outlets in Iberia (48 added in Spain in 2025; another count implies 552 at end-2024, a third quotes 600). Vulco: 290 in Spain and Portugal. Point S: 57 at end-2025, 72 by mid-2026. Confortauto (700+, 64 own, Hankook co-branded) belongs to Grupo Soledad, so its volume is already inside Soledad's wholesale volume and is not added again. Euromaster's older '500,000 tyres a year' web statement is outdated and not used.

Private versus commercial is a planning assumption of about 83% / 17% (private 14.30 + 1.50 + 0.45 + 1.18 = 17.43M; commercial 2.96 + 0.50 + 0.05 + 0.12 = 3.63M). No Spanish split is published. MITECO's passenger-car versus van split is by vehicle type, not by customer.

Latest signals (research, not checked unless stated): ADINE's Distripool shows consumer distribution +5.6% in 2025 (the headline is on Posventa; I did not open it) and +5.2% in the first quarter of 2026; GfK sell-out +7% in volume in 2025; Europool +5.5% to May 2026 (about 6.475M). Applying +5.6% to 21.06M gives about 22.2M for 2025 (research estimate, not a MITECO figure). Europool's all-season tyres grew over 10% and 19-inch and larger over 22% in 2024.

Wholesale cross-check (October 2026): Andrés, Soledad and NEX together plausibly carry 42–58% of the 14.7M layer. Nothing points to it being too high. See the Wholesale check tab for the figures, sources and caveats.

market.short: The ministry's producer register (as analysed by ADINE): 17.93M car tyres + 3.12M van, 4x4 and SUV tyres.
how: Spain's ministry (MITECO) keeps a register where producers and importers declare the new replacement tyres they place on the market. For 2024 it shows 24,559,740 tyres of all types.
ADINE, the tyre importers' association, analysed it: car tyres 17,934,194 + van, 4x4 and SUV tyres 3,124,549 = 21,058,743, reported by Posventa (checked).
These are tyres placed on the market by producers, so it is a sell-in measure used as a stand-in for the market.
market.src: MITECO producer register, ADINE analysis reported by Posventa (checked).

sure.w: Published register data, but the split comes from ADINE's analysis; the PDF's own unit rows differ (see the heads-up).

market.check: The MITECO PDF I opened lists different unit rows for the same two groups (cars 15,191,656 and vans / 4x4 / SUV 3,679,718, together 18.87M), and its unit rows do not add up to its own 24,559,740 total, while its tonnes do. The tonnes match ADINE's split. I kept ADINE's figures because they add up exactly. If you prefer the PDF's rows, the market would be about 18.9M. Not changed.
market.why: Spain has an official count: the ministry's register of tyre producers (MITECO), analysed by ADINE, records the new replacement tyres that producers placed on the Spanish market in 2024. It is a sell-in measure, used as a proxy for the market.
market.val: Sanity check: 21.06M ÷ 26.47M cars (ANFAC, quote kept) = 0.80 tyres per car, in line with Germany (0.83) in this dashboard. Caveat: the unit rows in the MITECO PDF do not add up to ADINE's figure; see the heads-up.

The research quotes it from Europneus. I could not find the Europneus release online, so I have not checked it.
“Pool” does not mean European premium: ETRMA members include Apollo, Hankook and Nexen, and Linglong joined on 4 November 2024 (research, not checked).

sure.w: Labelled published, but I could not find the release to verify it.

industry.why: The pool (Europool, the ETRMA member brands) reports its own Spanish sales through Europneus, so this is a reported figure rather than a model. It is quoted by the research.
industry.val: I could not find the Europneus release, so this is unchecked. A Goodyear Spain executive says import brands are "four in ten" tyres sold (sell-out basis, via Europneus, not checked), which would put the pool nearer 12.64M than 14.78M. The research suggests 40% as an upper sensitivity.

import.short: Calculated: the 6.28M gap between the market (21.06M) and the pool (14.78M).
how: The market is 21.06M and the pool supplied 14.78M. The gap of about 6.28M (about 30%) must come from outside the pool.
In the model it comes out of the chain: wholesalers sold 14.68M = 8.39M from the pool + 6.28M imports − 0.00M exports.
It is net non-pool supply, not gross imports. Asian consumer-tyre imports alone were about 13.4M, but they include pool brands made in Asia.

The model has no flow for imports going straight to the channels, so the whole gap is shown via wholesale. About 0.50M of it (online sellers and private labels) really goes direct and sits in the Direct box.
import.src: Calculated from the market and the pool. Not published.

sure.w: It depends on a market and a pool figure that are not like-for-like, and it is not published.

import.check: A conflicting claim: import brands are “cuatro de cada diez” (four in ten) of the tyres sold, according to Goodyear Spain's head of consumer sales via Europneus, on a sell-out basis (not checked). The research suggests showing 40% as an upper sensitivity.
import.why: Once the official market count and the pool's reported sales are fixed, whatever is left must have come from brands outside the pool. That residual is 6.28M (30% of the market), so it is only as good as those two figures.
import.val: Asian consumer-tyre imports were 13.4M in 2024 (ADINE, as quoted by the research, not checked), but they include Asian-made pool brands, so they cannot be compared directly. Goodyear's "four in ten" would make the non-pool part larger.

export.short: Set to zero: the register figure is already net of exports.
how: MITECO counts tyres placed on the Spanish market, so it is already net of exports.
That does not mean Spain exported nothing. The research puts possible re-exports of pool volume at 0.2–0.5M.

sure.w: A convention, not a measurement.

direct.short: About 30% of the market (6.38M) is assumed to reach the channels without a wholesaler.
how: The research estimates 5.88M of pool volume sold direct (manufacturer-owned and affiliated networks such as Euromaster, First Stop and Vulco, dealers and key accounts).
Plus 0.50M of non-pool imports bought direct by online pure players and autocentro private labels.
It adds up from the channels: 4.40 + 1.00 + 0.18 + 0.80 = 6.38M.

direct.why: Manufacturer-owned or affiliated networks (Euromaster, First Stop, Vulco), dealers and key accounts are supplied directly, while independent garages, the largest group of fitters, buy mainly through distributors. That is why 30% of the market (6.38M) is assumed to go direct. Online pure players and autocentro private labels add to it by importing directly.
direct.val: Not published; the research rates it low confidence. Euromaster España has 443 workshops in Spain (Motor16, checked), which shows how large the manufacturer-owned networks are. Best check: your own Spanish sell-in by account type.

how: The pool's 14.78M minus the 6.38M that goes direct leaves 8.39M for wholesalers.

The import box is the research's 4.1M estimate of non-pool wholesale imports (about 3.4M sold in Italy plus 0.7M re-exported), not customs imports: Italy imported 35.7M and exported 18.5M passenger-car tyres in 2024 (UN Comtrade, as quoted by the research), which include factory, original-equipment and intra-group flows. The export box is the research's 0.7M estimate of re-export by independent distributors. Online means the consumer buys online, not a gommista ordering through a wholesaler's B2B portal.
meta.scopeNote: The 27.0M is anchored on GfK's specialist-dealer sell-out (19.68M) divided by an assumed 72.9% specialist share. The research calls it passenger-car only, but GfK's earlier Italian releases include light-truck and 4x4/SUV tyres, so read it as a consumer-tyre figure like the other countries. The card header shows tonnes (MASE, all tyre types), which is not comparable. The research does not cover private versus commercial demand, so those boxes still need input.

channels.val: Replace with NIQ-GfK channel data for dealers and online if you have it. The quote kept is the older GfK series for specialists.

refs: Method (replaced with the Italy research file): the channel volumes follow the research's model of 72.9 / 15.7 / 2.6 / 8.8%, replacing the earlier benchmark of 68 / 12 / 3 / 17% on a 33M market. Only the specialist total has a measured anchor; the other three channels and every route split are modelled allocations.

Specialist anchor: NIQ-GfK, as quoted by the research in March 2026, put specialised tyre-dealer sales at 19.6M in 2025, down 0.4%, which implies 19.68M in 2024. I could not find that release. What I could confirm is the older GfK series for the same panel: 19.7M tyres in 2022, also down 0.4% (GfK, September 2023), covering passenger-car, light-truck and 4x4/SUV tyres. So the order of magnitude holds, but the scope may include light trucks.

Market size: 19.68M divided by a 72.9% specialist share gives 27.0M. The 69-77% sensitivity gives 25.6-28.5M. The research cross-checks it at about 0.65 tyres per car on a parc of about 41.3M cars (ACI/ACEA, as quoted, not checked) and expects 2025 to be flat at 26.8-27.0M. The earlier 33M converted MASE's 421,645 tonnes, which cover all tyre types.

Customs versus domestic balance: UN Comtrade (as quoted by the research, not checked) shows 35.735M HS 401110 passenger-car tyres imported (9.04M from China) and 18.467M exported in 2024. Net imports of 17.3M reflect Italy's role as a manufacturing and distribution hub, so customs data are not used in the import or export boxes.

Non-pool supply: the research quotes NIQ-GfK's extrapool share at 14.7% of specialist volume in 2025, up 26% in a year, which implies about 11.7% (about 2.30M tyres) in 2024. Adding online and other retail gives about 3.4M non-pool tyres consumed in Italy, plus 0.7M re-exported, so 4.1M. On 7 July 2026 the European Commission imposed definitive anti-dumping duties of 4.3% to 45.3% on Chinese passenger-car and light-truck tyres (confirmed, Eunews). China supplied almost 93M such tyres to the EU in 2024, a 28% share.

Wholesale versus direct is a modelled split: 13.2M of the 23.6M industry volume goes through wholesale and 10.4M direct, plus 4.1M non-pool imports, less 0.7M re-exported, gives 16.6M wholesale sold in Italy (about 61.5%) and 10.4M direct (about 38.5%). The 13.2M is a residual that reconciles the model, not an observed figure.

Wholesalers (checked): Fintyre's own site states over 6M tyres a year, 2 hubs, 10-12 warehouses and more than 50 brands, through three companies: Fintyre, Franco Gomme and Gexpo Tyre. Tyrepress reported Univergomma's 2023 revenue above 335M EUR (up 5%, car segment growing). Atoka lists Zuin as a tyre and auto-parts wholesaler in San Pietro in Gu with latest declared revenue of 89.4M EUR. Tyre Trends (May 2024) describes Magri Group as a national multi-brand distributor of car, truck and agricultural tyres working with the CDG and Kwik Fit networks.

Wholesale volumes are the research's PCR estimates, converted from all-category disclosures, not company figures: Fintyre about 4.5M (4.0-5.0M), Univergomma 3.1M (2.6-3.6M), Magri 1.5M (0.9-2.0M), Zuin 1.0M (0.8-1.3M), Pneus In 0.6M, Palmeri 0.45M, Intergomma 0.35M, regional importers about 1.2M combined. Not confirmed: Univergomma's 5M pieces in 2024 and 1M tyres in stock, Zuin's 86M EUR for 2024 and 500+ points of sale, Magri's 60% car share of revenue, and the Pneus In, Palmeri, Intergomma, Pneutec, Piùgomme and PR Sud details. Tagliabue Gomme Gross and Carlini Gomme, already on the list, are not covered by the research.

Latest signals (research, not checked): all-season tyres reached 31.6% of specialist volume in 2025, up from 21.8% in 2020, with all-season volume up 3.0%, summer down 1.8% and winter down 2.0%. Michelin's market indicator shows European replacement demand broadly stable through August 2026. Older carried-over note: trade claims of very high online volumes come from sponsored articles and were not used.

Wholesale cross-check (October 2026): Fintyre and Univergomma alone report about 5M tyres each, and the research run puts the named group near 68% of the 16.6M layer. If anything the layer looks slightly low. See the Wholesale check tab for the figures, sources and caveats.

toWs.source: Calculated, not published: ETRMA industry 4.90M minus the direct volume 3.13M. The direct volume is the research's 2.85M x 1.10 = 3.135M, rounded to 3.13M so the figures tie, and kept at that level on purpose: direct supply is largely manufacturer-owned networks such as BestDrive (Continental) and Euromaster (Michelin), central accounts and cross-border e-commerce, which do not grow just because ETRMA's figure is higher. The extra pool volume therefore goes via wholesale and, as the Export box shows, leaves again. The research's own split of the pool was 0.75M via wholesale and 2.85M direct (21% / 79% of 3.6M). At that ratio ETRMA's 4.90M would give 1.02M via wholesale, and wholesalers would sell only 1.07M in Austria, leaving little room beyond the named wholesalers, whose research estimates add up to about 0.8M. import.source: Research estimate (2024, range 1.4-2.1M for passenger cars) of non-pool supply that enters the wholesale layer, 1.70M x 1.10 = 1.87M for the consumer scope (range 1.54-2.31M). It is not gross customs imports: UN Comtrade (as quoted by the research, not checked) shows 9.056M passenger-car tyres imported in 2024, which includes original-equipment supply, distributor stock and re-export trade. The research did not re-estimate it for 2026. Replaces the earlier 1.70M.

export.source: Estimate, not published: it closes the flow so that the boxes add up, ETRMA industry 4.90M + imports 1.87M - market 4.95M = 1.82M. It holds two parts that cannot be separated: about 0.88M that the research estimates for re-export through wholesalers (0.80M for passenger cars x 1.10; range 0.66-1.10M), and about 0.94M by which ETRMA's pool figure is above the research's pool estimate on the same scope (3.96M). You chose to place that gap here, as for the Netherlands: pool volume invoiced to Austria and sold on abroad. The research says Austrian wholesalers re-export part of what they buy and that ARG exports about half its volume (the latter not confirmed). Customs show 1.296M passenger-car tyres exported in 2024 (as quoted by the research, not checked), but that does not bound this box: if ETRMA allocates by invoice-to country, tyres invoiced to Austria and delivered from foreign warehouses never cross the Austrian border. If the gap really belongs in the market or in imports, export would be about 0.88M (the market would be 5.89M, or imports 0.93M). The market is already net of export. Replaces the earlier 0.80M.

refs: Scope and method (rebuilt October 2026): the Austria flow now covers cars, SUV/4x4, vans and light trucks together as passenger-car replacement, which is ETRMA's PV scope as you define it, on a rolling-year basis (RY2026). The industry box is ETRMA's own Pool Market Data for Austria (4,899,304 tyres in RY2026), supplied by you. The rest comes from the research's 2024 Austria model, which covered passenger cars only (SUV tyres included, vans excluded), widened by 1.10 for vans and light trucks: market 4.5M becomes 4.95M, imports 1.70M becomes 1.87M and the direct volume 2.85M becomes 3.13M. The 1.10 is an assumption (Statistik Austria counts 581,147 lorries of all classes against about 5.29M cars at the end of 2025, 11%). Export (1.82M) is the balancing figure: ETRMA 4.90 + imports 1.87 - market 4.95. The channel shares of 72 / 18 / 3 / 7% are kept from the earlier benchmark (anchored on the German BRV split) and applied to 4.95M. No public Austrian source gives a sell-out total or a channel split.

Market size: the research found no complete 2024 or 2025 Austrian sell-out figure. The GfK retail panel supported by VRO recorded almost 3.6M tyres in 2018 and is not all-channel coverage (I could not open that source). Working range 4.3-4.7M for passenger cars (4.73-5.17M widened by 1.10 to the consumer scope). The parc supports it: the research quotes 5.23M passenger cars at the end of 2024 (Statistics Austria), and ORF reports 5.29M at the end of 2025, up 54,208. Tyres per car: 4.95M / 5.29M = 0.94 (the car-only 4.5M on about 5.2M cars was 0.87).

How ETRMA's figure fits the research (October 2026): your ETRMA table shows 4,899,304 tyres for Austria in RY2026 and 5,503,244 in RY2025 (-11.0%). The research's own estimate of the same layer, the major brands' supply, was 3.6M for 2024 on passenger cars, or 3.96M (range 3.52-4.29M) on the consumer scope, so ETRMA is about 0.94M (24%) higher and 0.61M above the top of the research's range. ETRMA alone is almost as large as the whole market (4.95M) before any non-pool imports. Bridge in million tyres: ETRMA gross pool 4.90 + non-pool and parallel imports 1.87 = 6.77 supplied; 4.95 is fitted in Austria, so 1.82 leaves again through wholesale (about 0.88 is the research's own re-export estimate and 0.94 is the gap). You chose this. The alternatives were the market at about 5.89M (1.11 tyres per car, 14% above the top of its scaled range of 4.73-5.17M) or imports at about 0.93M (40% below the bottom of their scaled range of 1.54-2.31M); the chosen route puts export about 65% above the top of its 0.66-1.10M range, the largest departure in relative terms, but it is the one that fits ETRMA being gross and swinging 11% in a year. Customs data cannot settle it: Austria's exports were 1.30M passenger-car tyres in 2024 (as quoted, not checked), but if ETRMA allocates by invoice-to country, tyres invoiced to Austria and delivered from abroad never cross the Austrian border. To confirm with ETRMA: that RY2026 means the 12 months to September 2026, whether the table allocates by invoice-to or ship-to country, why Austria fell 11% in a year, and that the PV category matches the cars, SUV/4x4, vans and light trucks you described.

Customs versus domestic balance: UN Comtrade (as quoted by the research, not checked) shows 9.056M HS 401110 passenger-car tyres imported and 1.296M exported in 2024. Net imports of 7.76M exceed the estimated sell-out because customs data include original-equipment supply, distributor stock and re-export, so they are not used in the import or export boxes. The export box can also exceed the customs figure if ETRMA allocates by invoice-to country.

Wholesale versus direct is a modelled split, not a published figure. The research's version (2024, passenger cars): 0.75M of the 3.6M pool via wholesale and 2.85M direct, plus 1.70M of non-pool supply, less 0.80M re-exported, gave 1.65M wholesale sold in Austria (about 37%) and 2.85M direct (about 63%). Here the direct volume is kept at the research's level widened by 1.10 (3.13M), and the extra pool volume goes via wholesale: 1.77M via wholesale + 1.87M imports - 1.82M export = 1.82M wholesale sold in Austria (37% of the 4.95M market), and 3.13M direct (63%). Keeping the research's 21 / 79% ratio instead would give 1.02M via wholesale, 3.88M direct and only 1.07M sold by wholesalers in Austria. Direct is broader than factory-to-shop. BestDrive is Continental-owned and Euromaster is Michelin-owned, so a large part of retail is supplied outside independent wholesale.

Wholesalers (checked): AUTO PLUS Reifen is a subsidiary of Wolfgang Denzel Auto AG and is described by the Denzel Group as one of Austria's leading tyre importers and wholesalers with more than 2,000 dealer partners (Denzel press release, September 2022; Reifenpresse, January 2023). Tire Network's own site calls it a wholesaler for tyres, rims and complete wheels in Austria with over 50,000 tyres in stock, ordered through a members-only B2B shop for dealers and fitting partners; it is registered in Vienna (founded 2022). ARG Reifengrosshandel GmbH is registered in Dornbirn (WKO).

Wholesale volumes are the research's estimates, not company figures: Auto Plus about 0.6M PCR tyres a year (range 0.45-0.8M), Tire Network about 0.15M (0.10-0.20M), ARG about 0.05M domestic (0.03-0.08M), Delticom's Autoreifenonline.at B2B about 0.10M. I could not confirm Auto Plus's 350,000-tyre pre-season stock or 1,500 peak orders a day, or ARG's roughly 50% export quota. Delticom is treated as cross-border supply, not as an Austrian wholesaler. These are passenger-car estimates set against the earlier 4.5M market and have not been rescaled to the consumer scope.

Retail network corrections (checked): Forstinger now states 69 branches and 68 specialist workshops (earlier page: about 111). Lucky Car took over 24 former A.T.U sites in February 2024 (more than 270 jobs) and had 44 locations before, around 70 afterwards per LEADERSNET (the research says 60+). A 2022 Continental release announced that Profi Reifen and Reifen John would be renamed BestDrive over about two years, with over 50 workshops. Point S: the research quotes over 60 service locations from its site, while a 2022 UTA release quoted 100.

Latest signals (research, not checked): Tyres Europe reports European consumer replacement tyres up 2% in H1 2026, with all-season up 9%, summer down 2% and winter down 5%. Austria's situational winter-equipment rule runs from 1 November to 15 April. The research expects a 2026 run-rate of 4.5-4.6M but does not treat it as a published figure.

Wholesale cross-check (October 2026, updated 26 Oct after colleague feedback and sales-team input): With the sales team's 0.6M for Reifen NL, the named domestic wholesalers add up to about 1.35–1.75M tyres, 74–96% of the 1.82M layer. That is plausible for a concentrated trade, but it rests on one unpublished team figure and on stock-turn assumptions for Auto Plus and Tire Network. Low confidence. See the Wholesale check tab for the figures, sources and caveats.

Austria update (26 Oct 2026, colleague feedback plus a new research run): the card now names Reifen NL, Tyrol Pneu and Interpneu as wholesalers; Point S, Top Reifen Team and EFR as buying groups; and Porsche Inter Auto, Pappas, Denzel and Unterberger as car-dealer groups. AUTO PLUS is now shown as 0.6–0.95M consumer tyres a year (derived from its stated 350,000-tyre stock and an assumed 2–3 turns a year), which replaces the earlier 0.45–0.8M above. Checked by us: Lucky Car 62 locations and just under €80M revenue in 2025 (Leadersnet, 24 Mar 2026); Point S's 2015 figures of 60 locations and a 17% consumer share, with 20% as a target (Auto & Wirtschaft, 1 Sep 2015); Porsche Inter Auto 'über 50 Autohäuser' (its employer profile). Everything else new is quoted by the research run and its pages were not re-opened. Reifen NL is shown at 0.6M passenger-car tyres a year, an estimate from the sales team that is not published or verified. No model number was changed.

refs: Scope and method (rebuilt October 2026): the Hungary flow now covers cars, SUV/4x4, vans and light trucks together as passenger-car replacement, which is ETRMA's PV scope as you define it, on a rolling-year basis (RY2026). The industry box is ETRMA's own Pool Market Data for Hungary (2,538,220 tyres in RY2026), supplied by you. The rest comes from the research's 2024 Hungary model, which covered cars and SUV/4x4 only, scaled by 1.099 for vans and light trucks (HTA 2018: 2.860M for cars, SUV and light commercial together against 2.602M for cars and SUV, so vans and light trucks were 9.0% of the consumer total): imports 1.10M becomes 1.21M and re-export 0.25M becomes 0.27M. The market (3.48M) is not scaled; it is the balancing figure, ETRMA pool 2.54 + imports 1.21 - re-export 0.27. The channel shares of 70 / 10 / 5 / 15% are kept from the earlier benchmark (anchored on the German BRV split) and applied to 3.48M. No Hungarian source publishes sell-out by channel.

HTA 2018 (confirmed): the Hungarian Tyre Association reported 3.1M tyres sold in 2018 (up 9.7%) through manufacturers' representatives, of which passenger-car 2.4M (up 9%), SUV 182,000 (up 23%) and light commercial 258,000 (up 5%) (444.hu, January 2019). Cars, SUV and light commercial together are 2.860M, which is the consumer scope used here; the rest of the 3.1M, about 0.24M, is other categories. This is a sell-in series, what the manufacturers' Hungarian representatives sold to wholesalers and retailers, so it leaves out parallel and other imports that do not pass through them and probably understates the whole market. I found no HTA unit figures later than 2018; its later releases give percentages only.

Cars and tyres per car (updated October 2026): KSH reports 4.37M passenger cars at the end of 2025, up 111,000 (2.6%) in the year, with an average age of about 16.5 years (confirmed). The research quotes 3.642M cars at the end of 2018 (not checked). Consumer-scope tyres per car: HTA 2018 sell-in 2.86M / 3.64M = 0.79; the new market 3.48M / 4.37M = 0.80; the pool alone 2.54M / 4.37M = 0.58 (the pool's Hungarian sales net of re-export, about 2.27M, would be 0.52). The pool has therefore not kept pace with a car stock about 20% larger, which fits the research's view that budget and non-pool brands took share, but the 2018 figure is manufacturers' sell-in only, so the market-per-car comparison is not like for like. The research's 2024 market (2.85M for cars and SUV/4x4, range 2.65-3.05M; 3.13M on the consumer scope) assumed weak replacement demand since the post-Covid price shock, citing an Apollo executive's roughly 30% decline comment (not checked). Its 2025 figure (about 2.80M) and 2026 run-rate (about 2.90M) for cars and SUV/4x4 are estimates; the Tyres Europe changes it quotes (down 2% in 2025, up 2% in H1 2026) are European, not Hungarian, and not checked.

How ETRMA's figure fits the research (October 2026): your ETRMA table shows 2,538,220 tyres for Hungary in RY2026 and 2,550,272 in RY2025 (-0.5%). The research's own estimate of the same layer, the manufacturers' Hungarian sales entities, was 2.0M for 2024 on cars and SUV/4x4, or 2.20M on the consumer scope, so ETRMA is about 0.34M (15%) higher. Bridge in million tyres: ETRMA gross pool 2.54 = pool sold in Hungary 2.27 + re-export 0.27; pool sold in Hungary 2.27 + non-pool and budget imports 1.21 = 3.48 market. The research's imports and re-export are unchanged (only scaled), so the market carries the extra 0.34M. You chose this. The alternatives were imports falling to about 0.87M or re-export rising to about 0.61M; each also sits outside the research's range, and by more in relative terms (imports 12% below the bottom of their scaled range of 0.99-1.43M, re-export 40% above the top of its 0.16-0.44M) than the market (3.48M, about 4% above the top of its scaled range of 2.91-3.35M). To confirm with ETRMA: that RY2026 means the 12 months to September 2026, that the table allocates by invoice-to country (which would include tyres invoiced to Hungary but delivered elsewhere), and that the PV category matches the cars, SUV/4x4, vans and light trucks you described.

Customs versus domestic balance: customs data are not used. Hungary is a major tyre production and export hub (the research quotes HTA: 34.1M tyres produced in 2022), so import and export statistics include original-equipment supply, factory output and re-export. The 1.21M import and 0.27M export boxes are the research's estimates of non-pool distributor flows (1.10M and 0.25M for cars and SUV/4x4), scaled by 1.099 for vans and light trucks.

Wholesale versus direct is a modelled split, not a published figure. The research sent 62.5% of the pool volume through distributors and 37.5% direct (1.25M and 0.75M of 2.0M). Applied to ETRMA's 2.54M that is 1.59M via distributors and 0.95M direct. Add 1.21M of non-pool imports (shown going through wholesale only) and take off 0.27M re-export: wholesalers sold 2.53M in Hungary (73% of the market) and 0.95M went direct (27%). The research's version was 2.10M and 0.75M (74 / 26).

Wholesalers (checked): AKH is a Hungarian family-owned company that says it sells more than one million tyres a year and had more than 200 reseller partners in its service programme (Vilaggazdasag 2021 and 2022). MARSO is a tyre wholesaler with more than 1,000 resellers and 30 stores in 2020, and 2019 revenue of HUF 27.3bn (Vilaggazdasag). Not confirmed: AKH's claims of 2,000 reseller partners and being the largest player, MARSO's 16 regional warehouses, the 2024 domestic sales of HUF 33.0bn (MARSO) and HUF 27.1bn (AKH), and Bridgestone's 2023 move of distribution to MARSO.

Caution on wholesaler volumes: the research estimates 0.65-0.80M PCR for AKH and 0.55-0.70M for MARSO. In 2022 AKH's deputy CEO put its market share at around 10% (Economx), which is hard to reconcile with 23-28% of the earlier 2.85M market (19-24% of the 3.48M now used), so treat these volumes as upper-end estimates. The player ranges were set against the earlier 2.85M market and have not been rescaled. The earlier note that MARSO holds exclusive Michelin and Bridgestone agreements is removed because I found no support for it.

Manufacturer layer: the research names Apollo, Bridgestone, Continental, Goodyear, Hankook, Michelin and Pirelli as having Hungarian sales entities (HTA, as quoted, not checked). They supply distributors and large accounts directly and sit behind the industry and direct boxes. The Gumi.hu network size differs: this page says 150+ service points, the research 100+ workshop stations. Left as is.

Wholesale cross-check (October 2026): AKH and MARSO together plausibly carry 60–95% of the 2.53M layer, and a bond document puts passenger-tyre wholesale at about 70% of the market, close to the dashboard's 73%. See the Wholesale check tab for the figures, sources and caveats.

market.short: The balancing figure: pool 2.54M + imports 1.21M − re-export 0.27M = 3.48M.
how: What reaches Hungarian fitters comes from two places: the ETRMA pool brands (2.54M, of which 0.27M is shipped on abroad) and non-pool and budget imports (1.21M).
The research's own 2024 market was 2.85M for cars and SUV/4x4 only (range 2.65–3.05M). Widened to include vans and light trucks (× 1.099) it is 3.13M (range 2.91–3.35M).

ETRMA's pool figure is 0.34M above what the research assumed for the pool (2.20M on the same scope). You chose to keep imports and re-export as the research had them and let the market absorb that gap.
market.src: Calculated from the ETRMA figure (published) and the research's import and re-export estimates (scaled). Not a published market size.

sure.w: No Hungarian market series exists for 2026. It is the sum of one published figure and two scaled research estimates, and it absorbs the gap between ETRMA and the research.

market.check: The market is not measured. If more pool volume is shipped on abroad than the 0.27M assumed, the market is lower by the same amount.
market.why: ETRMA's pool figure is now the one hard number for Hungary, so the market is built from the supply side: pool sold in Hungary plus non-pool imports. ETRMA is 0.34M above what the research assumed for the pool, and you chose to let the market, not imports or re-export, absorb that gap. It is the least strained place for it: it puts the market about 4% above the top of the research's scaled range (3.35M), whereas imports would fall 12% below the bottom of theirs and re-export would rise 40% above the top of theirs.

meta.boxNote: Boxes are the channels as named under "By channel". Switzerland has no tyre production, so the industry box is what the manufacturers' Swiss sales companies supply. The import box is the research's 1.80M estimate of non-pool supply entering wholesale (cross-border EU wholesalers, B2B platforms and online sourcing), not customs imports, which the research quotes at 7.15M passenger-car tyres for 2024. The export box is its 0.20M estimate of re-export. Online is the seller of record. Private and commercial are a planning assumption of about 75 / 25.
meta.scopeNote: The 6.5M is a model estimate (range 5.9-7.0M) for passenger-car and SUV/4x4 replacement tyres, light commercial excluded. It replaces an earlier 4.1M parc-based figure that also covered vans. No Swiss association publishes a unit total or a channel split, so every figure below the market is modelled, not published. Private versus commercial is a planning assumption of about 75 / 25, not data.
meta.walkNote: No Swiss association publishes a unit total or a channel split, so every figure is modelled. The import box is non-pool supply entering wholesale, not customs imports.

channels.why: No Swiss association publishes a channel split, so the research models about 65 / 23 / 2 / 10% of the 6.5M market.
channels.val: Nothing published to test it against. ESA's roughly 7,000 co-owner garages (Wikipedia, checked) support a large garage channel. Replace with your own Swiss channel data.

refs: Method (replaced with the Switzerland research file): the market and every flow and channel figure are modelled for passenger-car plus SUV/4x4 replacement tyres, light commercial excluded. The earlier benchmark shares (65 / 18 / 3 / 7% of a 4.1M parc-based figure) are replaced by the research's model of about 65 / 23 / 2 / 10% of 6.5M. No Swiss association publishes a unit total, a sell-out series or a channel split.

Market size: the 6.5M (range 5.9-7.0M) is anchored on customs, not on a published market figure. The research quotes UN Comtrade/WITS data for HS 4011.10: 7,151,750 tyres imported (USD 618M, about USD 86 a tyre, down 2%) and 265,043 exported in 2024, a net 6.89M. It deducts 0.04M for Liechtenstein, 0.15M for stock build and 0.20M for non-passenger-car use to reach 6.50M. I could not check any of these figures. The parc is 4.80M cars (BFS 2024, as quoted).

Plausibility caution: 6.5M on 4.80M cars is about 1.35 tyres per car a year. Austria is 0.87 and the Netherlands 0.85 in this dashboard, and the earlier Swiss figure was 0.88. Customs imports can include stock building, cross-border trade and tyres that never reach Swiss drivers, so the 5.9M low end of the range (about 1.23 per car) is still above the neighbours. Treat 6.5M as the research's central case, not a confirmed number.

Customs versus domestic balance: Switzerland produces no tyres and sits outside the EU customs union, so imports are the only supply. The research quotes Germany at 35.6% of 2024 import value (the 33% on the earlier page was the 2023 share) and 2025 imports of 7.40M. Both are as quoted, not checked. The earlier page's import price of about $62 a tyre, down 30%, is withdrawn because the research's customs data give about USD 86, down 2%.

Wholesale versus direct is a modelled split, not a published figure: 2.4M of the 4.9M industry volume goes through wholesale and 2.5M goes direct, plus 1.8M of non-pool supply, less 0.2M re-exported, gives 4.0M wholesale sold in Switzerland (62%) and 2.5M direct (38%). Direct means any route that bypasses an independent Swiss wholesaler, including the manufacturer-owned networks.

Wholesale layer, research throughput estimates (not company figures) adding to 4.00M: ESA 0.80M, cross-border EU wholesalers and B2B platforms 0.90M (the research names Pneuhage and Interpneu in Germany), online pure-players' sourcing 0.45M, manufacturer-affiliated wholesale 0.40M, Swiss Tyre Group 0.15M, Pneuhaus Leu 0.05M, Pneucore 0.03M, Interpneu AG 0.02M and a fragmented remainder of 1.20M.

Checked: ESA is a cooperative of the Swiss motor trade founded in 1930 in Burgdorf with about 7,000 co-owners (Wikipedia); it reported record sales of CHF 416.9M in its May 2022 results (Wirtschaftszeit), and Wikipedia gives CHF 445.3M for 2023. The research's 2024 figures (CHF 373.8M, 6,906 co-owners, 730 staff) do not match these and are not used. Swiss Tyre Group's own site describes a cooperation of independent tyre dealers founded in 2006 with 17 shareholders and 25 sales points that bundle purchasing (the research said 15 and 19, so the site is used).

Retail networks: Continental's release of 17 November 2022 confirms that Adam Touring and Pneu Egger, the two brands of Contitrade Schweiz AG, a 100% Continental subsidiary, were renamed BestDrive by Continental in a rollout planned for 2023, so the separate Adam Touring entry is merged. The research gives BestDrive 70+ workshops, Euromaster about 30 centres, First Stop 72+ and Premio Switzerland 85 partners; I could not check those counts. The research could not verify Point S Suisse, and Emil Frey and Bosch Car Service were not re-checked.

reifen.com belongs to Apollo (Apollo bought Reifencom GmbH in November 2015, European Rubber Journal and Tyrepress), not to Delticom, so it is now listed separately from ReifenDirekt.ch (Delticom). Pneuhage is a German group and the research found no verified Swiss subsidiary, so it is kept as a cross-border supplier only. Interpneu AG in Ballwil is a small Swiss wholesaler unrelated to Pneuhage's Interpneu.

Apollo's own presence (research, not checked): Apollo Tyres (Schweiz) AG in Baden is described as Apollo's Swiss sales company with a warehouse, trading under the former Maloya and Vredestein names. The research expects about 6.60M in 2025 and a similar 2026 run-rate; both are estimates with low confidence.

flows.scope: Passenger-car replacement tyres (car + SUV/4x4; excludes light commercial)

market.short: A customs-based estimate of 6.5M (range 5.9–7.0M). No Swiss body publishes a total.
how: Switzerland makes no tyres, so every tyre is imported. The research anchors on customs data (UN Comtrade / WITS, HS 4011.10, as quoted; I could not check them): 7,151,750 new passenger-car tyres imported and 265,043 exported in 2024, a net 6.89M.
It deducts 0.04M for Liechtenstein, 0.15M for stock building and 0.20M for non-passenger-car use.
market.src: Research estimate on customs data (quoted, not checked).

sure.w: Customs imports can include stock building, cross-border trade and tyres that never reach Swiss drivers.

market.check: 6.5M on about 4.80M cars is 1.35 tyres per car a year, well above Austria (0.87) and the Netherlands (0.85) here. Even the low end of the range (5.9M, about 1.23 per car) is above the neighbours. Treat 6.5M as the research's central case, not a confirmed number.
market.why: Switzerland makes no tyres, so customs imports are the natural anchor: 7.15M new passenger-car tyres in 2024. The research then removes exports, tyres for Liechtenstein, stock build and non-car use to reach what Swiss drivers consumed: 6.5M (range 5.9–7.0M). The customs figures are UN Comtrade/WITS as quoted by the research, not checked.
market.val: Sanity check: 6.5M ÷ 4.83M cars (BFS, quote kept) = 1.35 tyres per car, far above Germany (0.83) and Austria (0.86) in this dashboard. Even the 5.9M low end is 1.22, so the lower end of the research range looks more plausible.

industry.short: A research model: about 4.9M of the 6.5M is supplied by the manufacturers' Swiss sales companies.
how: Switzerland produces no tyres, so the pool figure is what the manufacturers' Swiss sales entities supply.

sure.w: Not published.

industry.why: Every tyre sold in Switzerland is imported, either by a manufacturer's Swiss sales entity or by an importer. The research models the manufacturers' entities as supplying about 4.9M (75% of the market).
industry.val: Not published. Replace with ETRMA's Switzerland pool figure if you can get it, as you did for the Netherlands.

toWs.short: Of the 4.9M, 2.4M is modelled as going through wholesale.
how: The research models 2.4M of the pool volume going through wholesale and 2.5M direct.

sure.w: Not published.

toWs.why: Manufacturer-owned networks are supplied directly (for example Continental's Contitrade Schweiz, whose Adam Touring and Pneu Egger brands became BestDrive), while independent garages and co-operatives such as ESA buy through wholesale. The research puts 2.5M (51% of the pool volume) direct and 2.4M via wholesale.
toWs.val: The BestDrive ownership fact is checked (Continental release, 17 Nov 2022); the volumes are modelled. ESA, the motor-trade cooperative, reported record sales of CHF 416.9M in 2022 (Wirtschaftszeit, checked), which shows a large wholesale layer but not the split.

import.short: About 1.8M of non-pool supply enters wholesale.
how: Mainly cross-border EU wholesalers and B2B platforms, plus the sourcing of online pure-players.

sure.w: Not published.

import.why: Brands outside the pool reach Swiss fitters through cross-border EU wholesalers and B2B platforms, and online pure players source abroad. The research puts that supply entering Swiss wholesale at 1.8M. It is not customs imports.
import.val: Customs show 7.15M passenger-car tyres imported in 2024 (as quoted by the research, not checked), which covers everything, so it cannot be used for this box.

export.short: About 0.2M is re-exported by Swiss wholesalers.
how: The research estimates 0.20M of re-export. Customs exports of 0.27M passenger-car tyres in 2024 (as quoted, not checked) are the reference.

sure.w: Not published.

export.why: Swiss wholesalers re-export a little, so the research includes a small estimate of 0.20M.

how: The pool's 4.9M minus the 2.4M that goes via wholesale leaves 2.5M direct.

wsDom.short: Calculated: pool to wholesale + imports − exports.

dst.note: The article gives the stock at 1 January 2025.

market.source: Estimate, not published: the balancing figure of the flow, ETRMA pool 11.49M + non-pool imports 8.0M - re-export 3.5M = 15.99M (about 16.0M; the research's range is 14.5-17.5M), for cars, SUV/4x4, vans and light trucks together (the ETRMA PV scope). It replaces the 14.36M of earlier today, which counted only 2.87M of non-pool tyres (the Chinese producers' 20% share, PZPO): Poland's own customs data show 7.03M Chinese car tyres imported in 2025, and Oponeo alone sold 4.73M tyres in Poland in 2025, 33% of 14.36M. At the dashboard's median non-pool share (28%) the market would be 15.96M, so the two methods agree; the unopened IndexBox figure of 16.945M (2024) sits at the top of the range. Sanity check: 15.99M divided by 21.08M active cars (Samar, end-2025) is 0.76 tyres per car (0.68 on the old figure).

industry.source: ETRMA Pool Market Data (Europe excl. Turkey, PV, by country, rolling year to September 2026), supplied by you: Poland RY2026 11,494,066 tyres, against 11,430,931 in RY2025 (+0.6%); rounded to 11.49M. This is pool members' sell-in, so it is gross: it may include tyres invoiced to Polish customers that are re-exported (about 1.0M by the research's estimate, inside the export box), and it is not domestic sales. Scope: ETRMA PV, which you confirm includes 4x4 and light trucks, i.e. cars, SUV/4x4, vans and light trucks. To confirm: whether the table allocates volume by invoice-to or ship-to country. PZPO's 'about 12M' passenger car tyres a year (Auto Swiat, Sept 2024) is most likely the same pool layer, not the market.

import.source: Poland reports importing 7.03M new car tyres from China in 2025 (WITS / UN Comtrade, HS 4011 10, units as reported by Poland; 6.94M in 2024; value USD 243M, about USD 35 a tyre; read by the research run, page not re-opened). Plus about 1.0M from other non-pool origins (my estimate, range 0.5-1.5M): about 8.0M non-pool tyres entering Poland in a year (range 7.0-9.0M). It is gross: it includes tyres that are shipped on again (counted in the export box) and some Chinese-made tyres of pool brands, which are already inside the pool figure, so it may be a little high. Vans (HS 4011 20) are not in the China figure. This replaces the 2.87M estimate from PZPO's 20% Chinese share, which is far below the customs data. It is assumed to feed Polish wholesalers, as in the other flows.

export.source: My estimate (range 2.0-5.0M), not published: about 0.75M sold abroad by Oponeo in 2025 (company figure; 0.76M in 2024, checked; its foreign shops are supplied from Poland), about 1.0M re-exported by wholesalers and hubs (including supply to foreign subsidiaries of groups such as Inter Cars; no volume is published), and about 1.75M of non-pool imports that arrive in Poland and are sold on to other countries. The model has one export box, taken off at wholesale level, so Oponeo's 0.75M is deducted here even though it is bought direct; the direct figures are gross of it. It is not factory exports: Poland exported 30.6M new car tyres in 2025 (WITS, mostly local factory output), which never enters the Polish pool figure.

toWs.source: My estimate (range 5.2-6.9M), not published: about 52% of the pool's 11.49M goes through wholesalers and distributors. It is the pool minus the direct deliveries, which the research builds bottom-up at about 5.5M: online sellers' pool purchases about 3.0M (Oponeo and Enis buy from manufacturers), fast-fit and workshop networks about 1.2M, dealers and OEM programmes about 0.7M, fleet tenders about 0.4M and other retail about 0.2M. No Polish source gives this split. Supply statements point to a mixed route: Premio sites are supplied directly from Goodyear Group warehouses, Euromaster says it buys directly from the producers, and Handlopex says it works directly with the manufacturers (research run, not re-opened).

ch.onl.tot.source: My estimate, low confidence: 45% of the market (7.20M). Oponeo sold 4.73M tyres in Poland in 2025 (company figure; 4.26M in 2024, checked) and about 4.9M in the rolling year (research run), Enis about 1.5-1.9M, and Allegro sellers, 24opony, OponyExpress, Autodoc and others an estimated 0.8-1.5M, which adds to 7.2-8.3M, so 7.20M is at the low end. Oponeo's own executive says online is 'about 40%' of sales (units or value not stated). Counted by seller of record, wherever the tyre is then fitted. Earlier today: 5.75M (40%) of 14.36M.

ch.onl.ws.source: Estimate, low confidence: about 56% via wholesale (4.00M). Oponeo and Enis hold direct accounts with manufacturers (online sellers' direct purchases about 3.2M in this box, including the 0.75M Oponeo sells abroad); the rest comes from wholesalers and importers of record, including online sellers' own import arms (Enis is the exclusive Polish distributor of Austone). No Polish source publishes procurement routes by channel.

ch.onl.dir.source: Estimate: channel total minus via wholesale (7.20M - 4.00M). Gross of Oponeo's 0.75M foreign sales, which the flow deducts in the export box.

ch.onl.prv.source: Estimate, low confidence: about 85% private (6.10M of 7.20M), the channel total minus the commercial part. About 22.6% of the market is commercial overall (3.61M): company, leasing and fleet cars and vans. Not published by channel.

ch.onl.com.source: Estimate, low confidence: about 15% commercial (1.10M of 7.20M): small businesses and fleets that order online.

ch.spec.tot.source: Balancing figure, low confidence: 46% of the market (7.39M). After online (45%), dealers (7%) and other retail (2%) it is what is left for specialists, fast-fit chains and independent garages. About 13,000 tyre-service workshops (PZPO, 2019) and networks such as Q Service Castrol (636 in its locator), Bosch Car Service (400+), Premio (167) and Euromaster (100+) show a large workshop base. In Germany this channel takes 71% (BRV 2024), but Poland's online share is far higher. Earlier today: 7.60M (53%) of 14.36M.

ch.spec.ws.source: Estimate, low confidence: about 81% via wholesale (6.00M). Independent garages buy mainly from wholesalers and parts distributors such as Inter Cars and Auto Partner; fast-fit networks buy partly direct (Premio from Goodyear Group warehouses, Euromaster directly from the producers; research run, not re-opened).

ch.spec.dir.source: Estimate: channel total minus via wholesale (7.39M - 6.00M).

ch.spec.prv.source: Estimate, low confidence: about 72% private (5.29M of 7.39M), the channel total minus the commercial part. About 22.6% of the market is commercial overall (3.61M): company, leasing and fleet cars and vans. Not published by channel.

ch.spec.com.source: Estimate, low confidence: about 28% commercial (2.10M of 7.39M). Fleet and leasing tyre work runs mainly through Euromaster, Premio, Pneuhage partners and independent garages.

ch.deal.tot.source: Benchmark estimate, low confidence: 7% of the market (1.10M). Raised from 5% because companies bought about 69% of the 597k new cars of 2025 (PZWLP, via Masterlease; research run, not re-opened), many of them leased and serviced at authorised workshops; kept far below Germany's 20% (BRV 2024) because Poland's car parc is old (average 16.2 years, Samar). Earlier today: 0.76M (5%) of 14.36M.

ch.deal.ws.source: Estimate, low confidence: about 36% via wholesale (0.40M). Dealers and OEM replacement programmes buy mostly from the manufacturers' Polish sales entities (about 0.70M direct).

ch.deal.dir.source: Estimate: channel total minus via wholesale (1.10M - 0.40M).

ch.deal.prv.source: Estimate, low confidence: about 64% private (0.70M of 1.10M), the channel total minus the commercial part. About 22.6% of the market is commercial overall (3.61M): company, leasing and fleet cars and vans. Not published by channel.

ch.deal.com.source: Estimate, low confidence: about 36% commercial (0.40M of 1.10M). Leasing and company cars are serviced at authorised workshops.

ch.ret.tot.source: Benchmark estimate, low confidence: 2% of the market (0.30M), unchanged share. No Polish source for hypermarkets, petrol stations or parts stores. Earlier today: 0.25M of 14.36M.

ch.ret.ws.source: Estimate, low confidence: about a third via wholesale (0.10M), the rest direct (0.20M) from manufacturers' key-account sales. No Polish source.

ch.ret.dir.source: Estimate: channel total minus via wholesale (0.30M - 0.10M).

ch.ret.prv.source: Estimate, low confidence: about 97% private (0.29M of 0.30M), the channel total minus the commercial part. About 22.6% of the market is commercial overall (3.61M): company, leasing and fleet cars and vans. Not published by channel.

ch.ret.com.source: Estimate, low confidence: about 3% commercial (0.01M of 0.30M). Retail is almost all private.

meta.boxNote: Boxes are the channels as named under "By channel". Industry is ETRMA pool sell-in (11.49M, rolling year 2026), gross. About 6.0M of it goes through wholesale and 5.49M direct (estimates). Imports are 8.0M non-pool tyres (customs data for China plus an estimate), of which 3.5M are re-exported, so wholesale sold in Poland is 10.5M and the market 15.99M. Channel sizes: online 45%, specialists and garages 46%, dealers 7%, other retail 2%. Online is probably the least certain: the named sellers alone nearly fill it. Everything except the pool figure is an estimate.
meta.scopeNote: Period: the pool is the rolling year RY2026 (the 12 months to September 2026); Poland's customs figures and Oponeo's company volumes are calendar 2025, so the flow mixes the two. Industry is ETRMA's Pool Market Data for Poland, 11,494,066 tyres, supplied by you (RY2025 11,430,931, +0.6%), covering cars, SUV/4x4, vans and light trucks together. Imports (8.0M) are Poland's reported 7.03M car tyres from China in 2025 plus about 1.0M from other non-pool origins; export (3.5M) is an estimate; the market (15.99M, range 14.5-17.5M) is industry plus imports less export. It replaces earlier today's 14.36M, which counted only 2.87M of non-pool tyres. Wholesale versus direct, the channel splits and private versus commercial are estimates built to add up, low confidence. The card header's older $1.77B is a value-only figure.
meta.walkNote: Industry is ETRMA's pool figure (11.49M), gross: about 6.0M goes to wholesale and 5.49M direct. Wholesale also takes 8.0M of non-pool imports (Poland's customs figure for China plus an estimate) and 3.5M is re-exported, leaving 10.5M sold in Poland, so the market is 15.99M. Online is 45%, specialists 46%, dealers 7%, other retail 2%, and about 22.6% of tyres go to companies and fleets. All splits are estimates built to add up.

channels.why: No Polish source publishes a channel split of the whole market. Online is set at 45% because Oponeo (about 4.9M tyres in Poland over the rolling year) and Enis (1.5-1.9M) alone make 6.4-6.8M of the 7.20M online box, and Oponeo's own executive says online is about 40% of sales. Dealers are 7% and other retail 2%; specialists and garages are what is left, 46%.
channels.val: An analyst puts Oponeo alone at about 25% of tyre sales (units or value not stated), BiznesRadar at 36%; at 4.73M tyres that is a market of about 19M or 13M. Oponeo's volume would be 31% of this 15.99M market and 68% of the online box, so online may be higher still. The other three boxes have no outside data.

refs: Scope and method (second research run, 28 Oct 2026): the Poland flow covers cars, SUV/4x4, vans and light trucks together, which is ETRMA's PV scope as you define it. Industry is ETRMA's Pool Market Data for Poland (11,494,066 tyres in RY2026), supplied by you. Imports (8.0M) are Poland's reported 7.03M car tyres from China in 2025 plus about 1.0M from other non-pool origins; export (3.5M) is an estimate; the market (15.99M, range 14.5-17.5M) is industry plus imports less export. The research's wholesale/direct split (6.0M / 5.49M), channel sizes (online 45%, specialists 46%, dealers 7%, other retail 2%), per-channel wholesale and direct, and private versus commercial (22.6%) are estimates built to add up, low confidence.

What changed from earlier today: the market moved from 14.36M to 15.99M. The earlier non-pool estimate (2.87M, from PZPO's 20% Chinese share) was a floor you chose to keep at 14.4M; the second run's evidence is Poland's customs data (7.03M Chinese car tyres in 2025; WITS / UN Comtrade, quoted by the research run and not re-opened by us) and Oponeo's volume (4.73M tyres in Poland in 2025, 33% of the old market). At the dashboard's median non-pool share of 28%, the pool would give 15.96M, so the two methods agree. The unopened IndexBox figure of 16.945M (2024) is at the top of the range. We could not open the WITS page ourselves; Eurostat Comext CN-8 data by partner and a Europool non-pool estimate would settle it.

How ETRMA's figure fits: your ETRMA table shows 11,494,066 tyres for Poland in RY2026 and 11,430,931 in RY2025 (+0.6%). PZPO reports its members' sales to distributors, so its 'about 12M' passenger car tyres a year (Auto Swiat, 16 Sep 2024, checked) is most likely the same pool layer. To confirm with ETRMA: that RY2026 means the 12 months to September 2026, that the table allocates by invoice-to country, and that PV matches the cars, SUV/4x4, vans and light trucks you described.

Oponeo (checked where noted): 2024 volume 5,015.77 thousand tyres in total, 4,259.12 thousand in Poland and 756.64 thousand abroad (ISBnews via inwestycje.pl, opened). 2025: 5.48M in total, 4.73M in Poland and 0.75M abroad, from the research run's quote of the same source, not re-opened; group revenue PLN 2,370.9M (+12.1%; domestic PLN 2,061.5M, abroad PLN 309.3M; automotive-accessories segment PLN 1,842.6M; BiznesRadar, opened). Q3 2025: 933,749 tyres (Strefa Inwestorow, opened). Q1 2026: 1,043 thousand tyres, +28.3% (BiznesRadar, opened); Q2 2026 volume flat year on year, stock PLN 858M, built ahead of the EU anti-dumping duties on Chinese tyres from July (DM PKO BP, 19 Aug 2026, opened). The research run puts the Polish volume at about 4.9M over the rolling year to mid-2026 (not re-checked).

Market share conflict: DM PKO BP puts Oponeo at about 25% of tyre sales (May 2025, units or value not stated), BiznesRadar at 36%, East Value (2021) at 30%. At 4.73M tyres these imply a market of 19M, 13M or 16M. On 15.99M Oponeo is 30% by units in 2025. Online share: Oponeo's executive says online is about 40% of sales (Autokult, research run quote), PKO BP (May 2025) had Oponeo at about 25% and Enis at about 9%, Parkiet (2023) offline 'still over 50%'.

Key customers (sell-out, by group): see the Poland card. Online: Oponeo about 4.7-4.9M, Enis (SklepOpon) about 1.5-1.9M (PLN 645.1M revenue in 2025, 624.3M in 2024; company claim of 1.5M tyres; research run, not re-opened). Wholesale: Handlopex revenue PLN 819.3M (2023), 847.4M (2024), 771.0M (2025; Aleo, checked), company claim over 3M tyres, 2.3-3.4M if all revenue were tyres at PLN 250-336 each; JMK PLN 193.4M (2025); Inter Cars' tyre volumes are not published (Polish sales PLN 8.12bn in 2025 across all products; research run). Networks: Premio 167 sites, about 1M customer visits a year; Euromaster over 100 stationary sites, 60+ mobile, 100+ fleet partners; Bosch Car Service 400+; Q Service Castrol 636 in its locator (670 claimed, 500 in 2022); Pneuhage Partner System 170+ partners. Network figures are mostly from company pages quoted by the research run; tyres per workshop are estimates.

Fleet and leasing (research run, not re-opened): PZWLP counts 288.7k long-term rental vehicles at end-2025 (+7.2%) and 261k in H1 2026 (+12.4%), on different scopes; companies bought about 69% of the 597k new cars of 2025. Commercial tyre demand is estimated at 3.0-4.5M (central 3.6M, 22.6%). Car parc: 21.077M active passenger cars at end-2025, 24.2M in CEPiK with 3.13M inactive records; average age 16.24 years (Samar via Otomoto); PZPM puts the updated parc at 15.3 years.

Mix (Oponeo, research run): all-season tyres about 28% of the market in 2025, budget models about 60% of all-season sales; winter about 40% in 2024. Rzeczpospolita (2016, dated): budget brands 53% of the Polish market. PZPO 2025 sell-in: passenger car +2%, SUV +18.8%, vans +7.9%; Q4 passenger car -9.8% (research run, not re-opened). ETRMA Q1 2026: Poland consumer tyres -2%, Europe +1% (BiznesRadar, opened).

Open items: (1) the WITS / Comtrade China imports page and Eurostat Comext CN-8 partner data; (2) a Europool non-pool or total figure for Poland; (3) Oponeo's and Enis's 2025 volumes at source; (4) tyre volumes of Inter Cars, Auto Partner and Moto-Profil; (5) a PZPO or Samar channel split; (6) the EU anti-dumping duties of 4.3-45.3% on Chinese car and light-truck tyres from 8 July 2026 (EUNews, checked earlier) will cut non-pool imports and distort the RY2026 and RY2027 stock flows.
flows.scope: Consumer replacement tyres (cars, SUV/4x4, vans and light trucks)

market.short: Pool 11.49M + non-pool imports 8.0M - re-export 3.5M = 15.99M, about 16.0M. An estimate, range 14.5-17.5M.
how: Europool's pool sell-in for Poland is 11.49M in the rolling year to September 2026 (published, supplied by you).
Poland reports importing 7.03M new car tyres from China in 2025 (customs data), plus about 1.0M from other non-pool origins (my estimate): about 8.0M non-pool tyres entering.
About 3.5M leave again: Oponeo's foreign sales (0.75M, company figure), about 1.0M re-exported by wholesalers and hubs, and about 1.75M of non-pool tyres in transit (estimates).
11.49M + 8.0M - 3.5M = 15.99M. It replaces earlier today's 14.36M, which counted only 2.87M of non-pool tyres.
market.src: Calculated from the Europool figure (published), a customs-based import figure and two estimates. Not a published market size.

sure.w: Two published figures, but how much of the Chinese imports stays in Poland and how much is re-exported are estimates. The plausible range is 14.5-17.5M.

market.check: PZPO says Chinese producers hold about 20% of passenger car tyres, which on the pool base is about 2.4M, against 7.03M in the customs data; some Chinese-made tyres are pool brands' own, and some are re-exported. At the dashboard's median non-pool share (28%) Poland would be 15.96M, so the two methods agree. The unopened IndexBox figure of 16.945M (2024) is at the top of the range. You earlier chose 14.4M; this is the evidence that moved it.
market.why: Europool's pool figure is the one hard number, so the market is built from the supply side as for Hungary, Austria and the Netherlands: pool plus non-pool imports less re-export. The earlier non-pool estimate (PZPO's 20% Chinese share) looks too low next to Poland's own customs data and next to Oponeo's volumes: Oponeo alone sold 4.73M tyres in Poland in 2025, 33% of the old 14.36M, while online sellers as a whole are 40-45%.
market.val: Tyres per car: 15.99M / 21.08M active cars (Samar, end-2025; CEPiK's 24.2M includes 3.13M inactive records) = 0.76, against 0.68 on the old figure. Hungary is 0.80, the Netherlands 0.85 and Austria 0.87 in this dashboard, and Poland's cars are old (16.2 years on average), which pulls it down. Oponeo would be about 31% of this market; analysts put it at 25% (DM PKO BP) and 36% (BiznesRadar), which at 4.73M tyres means a market of about 19M or 13M, so the range stays wide.

industry.short: ETRMA's own number for Poland (rolling year 2026), supplied by you.
how: ETRMA's Pool Market Data table, which you supplied, shows Poland RY2026 = 11,494,066 tyres (RY2025: 11,430,931, +0.6%).
It is the pool members' sell-in for cars, SUV/4x4, vans and light trucks together (ETRMA passenger vehicles, as you confirmed).
It is gross: it may include tyres invoiced to Polish customers and shipped abroad (about 1.0M by the research's estimate, deducted in the export box), so it is not Polish domestic sales.
Rounded to 11.49M. PZPO's 'about 12M' passenger car tyres a year (2024) is most likely the same layer, not the market.
industry.src: ETRMA Pool Market Data, supplied by you (screenshot).

sure.w: Published ETRMA data. Still to confirm: that RY2026 means the 12 months to September 2026, and whether ETRMA allocates by invoice-to or ship-to country.

industry.check: If ETRMA allocates by invoice-to country, tyres invoiced to Poland but delivered elsewhere are inside this figure; the model removes about 1.0M of them in the export box. Each 0.1M more or less moves the market by 0.1M.
industry.why: It is ETRMA's own published pool figure, supplied by you. The research had no estimate of this layer, so nothing is replaced.
industry.val: Check it against the ETRMA table (quote kept). PZPO's 'about 12M' (Auto Świat, Sept 2024) is in the same range, which supports reading it as the pool layer.

import.short: About 8.0M non-pool tyres enter: Poland's customs figure for China (7.03M) plus about 1.0M from elsewhere.
how: Poland reports 7.03M new car tyres imported from China in 2025 (6.94M in 2024; HS 4011 10, units; USD 243M, about USD 35 a tyre, i.e. budget tyres).
Plus about 1.0M from other non-pool origins (my estimate, range 0.5-1.5M): about 8.0M in total (range 7.0-9.0M).
It is gross: it includes tyres that are shipped on again (see Export) and some Chinese-made tyres of pool brands, which are already in the pool figure. Vans (HS 4011 20) are not included.
import.src: China figure: WITS / UN Comtrade as reported by Poland, quoted by the research run (page not re-opened). The rest is my estimate.

sure.w: The customs figure is published but not re-checked by us; how much of it is non-pool replacement supply is an estimate, and pool brands' Chinese-made tyres may be counted twice.

import.check: PZPO says Chinese producers hold about 20% of passenger car tyres (about 2.4M on the pool base). Customs data show 3 times as many arriving. Both can be true if PZPO's share is rounded and covers only its base, and if much of the customs volume is re-exported or is pool brands' own output. Eurostat Comext CN-8 data by partner, or a Europool non-pool figure for Poland, would settle it. Poland's total car-tyre imports were 22.9M in 2025; the 15.9M from other countries are not counted here, since most are pool brands delivered by their sales entities or in transit.
import.why: Poland's own customs data are the only hard volume for non-pool supply. The earlier 2.87M (PZPO's 20% share) was an estimate for lack of anything better, and it sits far below the customs figure. The 1.0M for other origins is a placeholder.
import.val: The China volume is checkable at WITS or Comext (quote kept). The rest is not: best check is your own Polish sell-in against the share you think pool brands hold, or Europool's non-pool estimate.

export.short: About 3.5M leave Poland again, re-exported or sold abroad: my estimate (range 2.0-5.0M).
how: Oponeo sold 0.75M tyres abroad in 2025 (company figure; 0.76M in 2024, checked). Its foreign shops are supplied from Poland.
About 1.0M more is re-exported by wholesalers and hubs, including supply to foreign subsidiaries of groups such as Inter Cars (no volume is published).
About 1.75M of the non-pool imports are in transit: they arrive in Poland and are sold on to other countries.
The model has one export box, taken off at wholesale level. Oponeo's 0.75M physically comes from its direct purchases, so the direct figures are gross of it.
export.src: My estimate built on Oponeo's company figure. Not published.

sure.w: Only Oponeo's 0.75M is a company figure; the rest are estimates.

export.why: Polish wholesalers, online sellers and hubs sell to Germany, Czechia, Slovakia, the Baltics, Ukraine and others, and some Chinese tyres only transit Poland. Nobody publishes the total. Customs exports are not used: Poland exported 30.6M new car tyres in 2025, mostly local factory output that never enters the Polish pool figure.
export.val: Not published. Because the pool figure is gross, any re-export above this estimate would lower the market by the same amount. Best check: Comext exports by partner with the factory output removed, or your own view of Polish hubs' foreign sales.

toWs.short: About 6.0M (52%) of the pool goes into wholesale: my estimate.
how: Direct deliveries are built bottom-up at about 5.5M: online sellers about 3.0M, fast-fit and workshop networks about 1.2M, dealers and OEM programmes about 0.7M, fleet tenders about 0.4M, other retail about 0.2M.
The rest of the 11.49M, 6.0M, goes through wholesalers and distributors (range 5.2-6.9M).

sure.w: A bottom-up estimate; nothing published confirms the split.

toWs.why: No Polish source gives it. Supply statements point to a mixed route: Premio sites are supplied directly from Goodyear Group warehouses (Fleet Derby), Euromaster says it buys directly from the producers (Auto Świat) and Handlopex says it works directly with the manufacturers (research run, not re-opened). Independent garages buy mainly from wholesalers and parts distributors.
toWs.val: Not published. PSO's CEO wrote in 2019 (checked) that a few wholesalers remain, the two largest each selling well above 2M tyres a year and the others 0.7-1.5M. That does not contradict 6.0M of pool tyres through wholesale, but it is seven years old. Best check: your own Polish sell-in by account type.

how: The pool's 11.49M minus the 6.0M that goes to wholesalers leaves 5.49M direct from the manufacturers (and their own networks) to the channels.
Bottom-up: online sellers about 3.0M, networks about 1.2M, dealers about 0.7M, fleet tenders about 0.4M, other retail about 0.2M.
direct.src: Calculated from the industry and to-wholesale figures.

sure.w: Only as good as the wholesale split it is built from.

direct.why: Large online sellers, manufacturer-owned networks, dealers and fleet tenders buy straight from the manufacturers' Polish sales entities. The research sets this at about 5.5M, which is the pool minus the wholesale part.
direct.val: Not published. Oponeo and Enis alone have direct accounts for most of the online part. Best check: your own Polish sell-in by account type.

wsDom.short: Calculated: pool to wholesale + imports - export = 10.5M.
how: Wholesalers sold 10.5M in Poland: 6.0M from the pool + 8.0M imports - 3.5M export (66% of the market).
From the other side: market 15.99M - direct 5.49M = 10.5M. The two agree.

sure.w: Built from model estimates; two thirds of it is imports.

wsDom.val: Cross-check with named wholesalers: Handlopex (revenue PLN 771-847M, about 2.3-3.4M tyres if all revenue were tyres; its own claim is 3M, all tyre types), JMK (about 0.5-0.8M) and Inter Cars (tyres cannot be separated) add up to about 3.3-6.5M, 31-62% of this layer. The rest would be smaller regional wholesalers and importers of record, including online sellers' own import arms.
